tops.title: Phase 2: Context Manager — Rich Prompts + Hybrid RAG

tops.title: Phase 3: Multi-Agent Pipeline + Chrome MCP Verification
tops.description:
Transform execution from single-agent fire-and-forget into a multi-stage pipeline. After Claude Code implements a task, Chrome MCP auto-opens the UI, tests the feature visually, and reports pass/fail. Failed tasks feed errors back to Claude Code for auto-retry (max 3 attempts).

tops.title: Phase 4: Parallel Execution + SSE Streaming
tops.description:
Run multiple agents concurrently on independent tasks. Replace 5-second polling with Server-Sent Events for real-time progress. Build dependency graph to determine which tasks can safely execute in parallel.

Impact: 2-4x faster feature implementation, instant status updates.

tops.title: Docker-Aware Watchdog Pause During VM Restart

When a user restarts the Colima VM from the /docker page, all Docker-based services go down for 20-60 seconds. tops.title: BUG: AutoPilot stops after first task — does not chain to next task
tops.description:
# AutoPilot Execution Engine Redesign

## Problem
The AutoPilot in `FeatureExecutionPanel.tsx` runs one task and stops — doesn't chain to the next task. This is a fundamental architectural issue with the execution engine.

## Root Cause
The execution chain uses **recursive `setTimeout` closures** across React re-renders:
- 5 tightly-coupled functions: `executeNext`, `pollForCompletion`, `handleAutoPilotSuccess`, `handleAutoPilotFailure`, `handleStartExecution`
- All defined as `const` inside component body (no `useCallback`), recreated every render
- `setTimeout` callbacks hold stale reference

## Solution

items.title: M5 — reset-failed-tasks rate limit keyed per-IP not per-queue/principal
items.description:
## QA finding (security MEDIUM)

`api/execution.py:~1462` `@limiter.limit('5/minute')` keys on client IP. Behind the local proxy callers share an IP — one abuser exhausts the budget for everyone; a distributed caller bypasses it.

## Fix
Key the limiter on `queue_id` or the authenticated principal.

items.title: M4 — detect_exhaustion bare '429'/'529' substrings false-positive
items.description:
## QA finding (code-reviewer MEDIUM)

`utils/exhaustion_detector.py` `_GENERIC_429_SIGNALS`/`_OVERLOADED_SIGNALS` contain the bare strings `429`/`529`, matched with plain `in` against 4 KB of subprocess output. Any file path / line number / SHA fragment containing 429 (e.g. `Foo.tsx:429`) triggers a false exhaustion classification -> queue wrongly paused into WAITING_RESET.

## Fix
Anchor to HTTP-status context (`\b429\b` with status keyword) or remove the bare numeric substrings — the JSON/HTTP-status paths already catch the real signal.

items.title: M3 — status/state column drift between save_queue and transition_state
items.description:
## QA finding (code-reviewer MEDIUM)

`transition_state` validates off `record.state or record.status`; `save_queue` (and the S4 direct-mutation safety-fallback sites) write only `record.status`. After a fallback mutation the two columns drift; a later rehydration validates a transition off a stale column and can wrongly reject a legal move.

## Fix
`save_queue` must mirror `record.state = queue.status.value`.

items.title: M2 — transition_state nulls pauseReason on every non-pause transition
items.description:
## QA finding (code-reviewer MEDIUM)

`utils/autopilot_repository.py` `transition_state` writes `record.pauseReason = new_reason`; for running/completed/aborted transitions `new_reason` is None, so the DB column is cleared. The in-memory mirror only clears pause_reason for pause states — memory and DB diverge, post-incident 'why was this paused' context is lost.

## Fix
Gate the pauseReason write the same way the in-memory mirror does.

items.title: M1 — recovery banner 'retry-failed' calls plain /resume, not retry_failed=true
items.description:
## QA finding (code-reviewer / security MEDIUM)

`AutoPilotRecoveryBanner.tsx:~496` maps the `retry-failed` action to a plain `POST /resume`. S3 (CB-2796) shipped `reset-failed-tasks` and `resume?retry_failed=true` precisely for this; AutoPilotFloatingBar uses them but the banner does not. A queue with only failed+completed tasks gets a 409 the banner silently swallows (`if (res.ok)` only). Headline feature unreachable from one of its two UIs.

## Fix
Banner -> `resume?retry_failed=true`; surface 409 to the user.

items.title: B5 — failing test: CB-2792 systemic-window constant not reconciled with S6
items.description:
## QA finding (failing test)

S6 (CB-2799) changed `_SYSTEMIC_FAILURE_WINDOW_SECONDS` 60.0 -> 1800.0. `tests/test_cb2792_systemic_failure.py::test_threshold_constant_matches_design` still asserts `== 60.0` => suite is RED (180 pass, 1 fail). The CB-2793 commit message claims '157 passed' — the failing file was either excluded or committed knowingly red.

## Fix
Reconcile the test with the consecutive-failures design from CB-2799 (update or remove the stale duration-window assertion). Verify the full AutoPilot suite is green.

items.title: B2 — state machine rejects idempotent self-edges (running->running)
items.description:
## QA finding (code-reviewer HIGH)

`models/autopilot.py` `_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` has no self-edges. After a swallowed DB-write failure leaves in-memory status at RUNNING, the resume-after-pause path calls `_transition(RUNNING)` => `running->running` => `IllegalStateTransitionError`. `clear_recovery_state` already carries a `paused->paused` special-case workaround — a symptom of this gap. Violates S4's (CB-2797) own 'do not swallow IllegalStateTransitionError' contract.

## Fix
Treat `from == to` as a no-op success in `is_transition_allowed` (or add explicit self-edges). Remove the clear_recovery_state workaround. Unit test each self-edge.

items.title: B1 — off-by-one defeats circuit-breaker abort recommendation
items.description:
## QA finding (code-reviewer HIGH)

`api/execution.py:1070` `_suggested_action` uses `auto_resume_attempts > _AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS`. Every other site was changed to `>=` in S1 (CB-2794). When the breaker trips the counter stays at MAX (3), so `3 > 3` is False and recovery-status returns `suggested_action='resume'`. The AutoPilotRecoveryBanner then shows a green 'Resume now' button instead of 'Abort' for exactly the runaway-token-burn scenario S2 (CB-2795) exists to stop.

## Fix
Change `>` to `>=` at `execution.py:1070`. Add a unit test asserting suggested_action=='abort' when attempts==MAX.

items.title: Scope get_or_load_queue to requesting project + redact last_error in API responses
items.description:
CB-2793 Security MEDIUM-2 follow-up.

Two related concerns:

1. `get_or_load_queue` loads any queue by ID without checking that the queue belongs to the project the caller is authorized for. A caller with a valid internal token can read/mutate queues from other projects by guessing queue IDs. Needs auth-scope enforcement (project-ownership check).

2. `last_error` on queue status responses may contain unsanitised error text from subprocess output. The same redaction used in the audit log (`_redact_error`) should be applied before returning `last_error` in API response payloads.

Requires broader auth-scope design work — tracking here for prioritisation.

items.title: Tune redaction regex breadth in audit log event sanitiser
items.description:
CB-2793 Security MEDIUM-1 follow-up.

The regex used to strip secrets from `last_error` / audit event payloads (`Bearer ...`, `sk-...`, `api_key=...`) may not cover all token formats in use (e.g. Anthropic API keys, session tokens). Needs a targeted audit of all formats that appear in Claude CLI output and a revised regex suite with corresponding tests.

This is a tuning concern with no acute exposure (errors are already partially redacted); file as MEDIUM for scheduling.

items.title: Refactor pause_reason to a proper enum/Literal type
items.description:
CB-2793 code review MEDIUM-3 follow-up.

`pause_reason` is currently an untyped `str` field scattered across `AutoPilotQueue`, `_transition`, `resume_queue`, `_recovery_tick_once`, and the API layer. The raw string `"manual"`, `"manual_cleared"`, `"manual_circuit_breaker"` etc. are used without a shared constant.

**Work:** introduce a `PauseReason` `Literal` or `StrEnum`, replace all bare string literals, add mypy enforcement.

Mechanical refactor — no behaviour change.

items.title: S6 — Token-exhaustion detection robustness (tail-window + systemic-window)
items.description:
## Bug

Two windowing problems in token-exhaustion detection:

**(a) Tail-window too small.** `detect_exhaustion_from_session` scans the
last 80 lines / 4 KB of CLI output. Claude CLI can dump 40-200 KB of
tool output AFTER an internal HTTP error. The token-exhaustion marker
(`rate_limit_error`, `usage limit`, `429`, etc.) scrolls out of the window.
Detector returns None. Task is marked `failed` instead of triggering
waiting_reset pause.

**(b) Systemic-failure window too short.** When the primary detector
misses, `_is_systemic_failure` (line 1171-1231) is supposed to catch
"3 identical failures in 60 s" via `_SYSTEMIC_FAILURE_WINDOW_SECONDS=60`.
Tasks run 2-15 minutes. Three failures in 60 s is mathematically
impossible at this cadence. LINK-124 burned through 7 sequential
failures over ~80 minutes; the heuristic never fired.

## Scope

1. `terminal_service` adds an exhaustion-signal buffer per session: any
   line matching the JSON regex `{"type": "error", ...}` OR the
   signal-set regex is appended to a dedicated list regardless of
   position in the stream. Feed THIS to `detect_exhaustion` instead of
   relying on the tail window.
2. Replace the duration-based systemic threshold with a
   **consecutive-failures** heuristic: 3 consecutive failures with the
   same normalised error AND no successes in between → category
   `unknown_systemic`, pause queue. Duration-independent.
3. Keep the duration-based heuristic as a secondary defense — widen
   `_SYSTEMIC_FAILURE_WINDOW_SECONDS` from 60 to 1800 (30 min).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New unit test: `test_exhaustion_detected_when_marker_buried_in_long_output`
      — feed 200 KB of output where the marker is in the first 4 KB,
      assert detection succeeds.
- [ ] `test_systemic_failure_three_consecutive_minutes_apart` — three
      failures 5 minutes apart with no success between, assert detector
      fires.
- [ ] `test_systemic_failure_cleared_by_success` — failure / success /
      failure / failure / failure should NOT trip (success cleared the
      streak).
- [ ] LINK-124 retrospective: re-feed the 7 captured outputs through the
      new detector and verify at least 1 would have triggered
      waiting_reset (proving the fix actually helps).

## Lineage

Discovered by general-purpose + code-reviewer agents during LINK-124
deep-dive (RC4). Most isolated of the six — can ship in parallel with
others once S1 (counter persistence) is in.

items.title: S5 — Single source of truth for state in recovery-status; fix clear_recovery_state no-op
items.description:
## Bug

`api/execution.py:1031-1119` (recovery-status endpoint) reports queue
state from three different sources:
- `auto_resume_pending` list hard-codes `"state": "waiting_reset"`
  regardless of actual queue.status (line 1102).
- `zombie` list hard-codes `"state": "running"` (line 1090).
- Backward-compat `queues` list reads `queue.status.value` from memory.

A queue that's `paused` in DB can appear as `running` in `zombie`,
`waiting_reset` in `auto_resume_pending`, and `paused` in `queues` —
all in the same response. UI consumers pick whichever they read first
and misrepresent state.

`clear_recovery_state` (line 889-891) is a one-liner:
```python
self._recovered_queue_ids.discard(queue_id)
```
Doesn't touch DB, doesn't cancel auto-resume timer, doesn't remove from
`_queues` or `_zombie_queue_ids`. Returns `{ok:true}` (line 1126) while
the queue keeps ticking. False UX promise.

## Scope

1. recovery-status: always derive `state` from a single helper
   `_serialize_queue(queue)` that reads `queue.status.value` (in-memory
   after `get_or_load_queue`). No hard-coded overrides.
2. `clear_recovery_state` actually clears: cancel auto-resume timer if
   live, remove from `_recovered_queue_ids` AND `_zombie_queue_ids`,
   transition queue to `paused` with `pause_reason='manual_cleared'`,
   persist.
3. `get_queue_status` adds DB fallback via `get_or_load_queue`
   (currently returns 404 for DB-only queues — line 2226).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `recovery-status` returns the same `state` for a queue across all
      three sub-lists (`recoverable`, `zombie`, `auto_resume_pending`),
      and that state matches the DB row.
- [ ] `clear_recovery_state` post-call: queue is `paused` in DB,
      auto-resume timer cancelled, not in `_zombie_queue_ids`.
- [ ] `get_queue_status(qid)` on DB-only queue returns full status
      (not 404).

## Lineage

Discovered by debugger + code-reviewer during LINK-124 deep-dive (RC5, RC6).
Depends on S4 for the transition primitive.

items.title: S4 — Canonical state transitions via transition_state() — eliminate 16 direct mutations
items.description:
## Bug

`transition_state` (`autopilot_repository.py:374-440`) was introduced as
"the only authorised path to write status". In practice, **16 call sites
in `autopilot_queue_service.py` directly mutate `queue.status = X`**
(lines 1004, 1023, 1034, 1105, 1122, 1163, 1192, 1226, 1258, 1852, 2077,
2089, 2311, 2513, 2607, and `pause_queue:2311`). Every authorised call
is wrapped in `try/except IllegalStateTransitionError: log+continue`.

Result:
- The allow-list at `models/autopilot.py:69-86` enforces nothing.
- In-memory dataclass advances even when DB write fails or transition
  is illegal.
- DB and memory drift silently.
- `pause_queue` skips `transition_state` entirely → no STATE_TRANSITION
  audit event for manual pauses.

## Scope

1. Make `transition_state` write DB FIRST (atomic with event) then mutate
   memory ONLY on success. If DB write fails, memory is NOT mutated.
2. Replace every `queue.status = X` mutation with
   `await self._transition(qid, X, reason)`.
3. `IllegalStateTransitionError` becomes a real failure (not swallowed).
   The 16 callers must either know the transition is legal (most do —
   they're well-defined state-machine moves) or handle the error
   explicitly.
4. `pause_queue` routes through `transition_state` (currently bypasses it).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Zero direct `queue.status = X` mutations remain in `autopilot_queue_service.py`
      (enforced by lint rule or test that greps the file).
- [ ] All state changes appear in `AutoPilotEvent` with type `STATE_TRANSITION`.
- [ ] DB and in-memory `queue.status` agree at all times (verified by
      `test_transition_atomicity` — kill the DB mid-transition, assert
      memory not mutated).
- [ ] `pause_queue` emits a STATE_TRANSITION event.

## Lineage

Discovered by code-reviewer agent during LINK-124 deep-dive. Largest
refactor in this feature — sequenced last among the must-haves so smaller
fixes don't have to land on shifting ground.

items.title: S3 — Resume endpoint contract + retry failed tasks (unblocks LINK-124)
items.description:
## Bug

Two issues collide:

**(a) `_find_next_pending` only matches `TaskStatus.PENDING`.** With all
remaining tasks `FAILED` (e.g. LINK-124 has 15 completed + 7 failed),
`pending_orders` is `[]`, `_find_next_pending` returns None,
`resume_queue` returns False (line 2394), API returns 400. The user
literally cannot resume their feature without DB surgery.

**(b) Resume endpoint returns 400 for every failure mode.** Missing
queue, wrong state, breaker-tripped, no pending tasks all collapse to
the same generic 400 with no `pause_reason` or `auto_resume_attempts`
in the body. UI cannot tell user *why* and *what to do*.

## Scope

1. New endpoint: `POST /api/execute/queue/{queue_id}/reset-failed-tasks`.
   Marks all `failed` tasks in the queue back to `pending`, clears
   their `failureReason`. Returns `{reset_count, task_ids}`.
2. New endpoint optional flag on resume:
   `POST /api/execute/queue/{queue_id}/resume?retry_failed=true` —
   atomically resets failed → pending, then resumes. Saves a round trip.
3. Resume endpoint contract:
   - 404 NOT_FOUND — queue does not exist in DB.
   - 409 CONFLICT — wrong state or breaker tripped. Body includes
     `pause_reason`, `auto_resume_attempts`, `current_index`,
     `pending_count`, `failed_count`, `suggestion`.
   - 200 OK — resumed.
4. Frontend `AutoPilotFloatingBar.tsx`: when 409 received with non-zero
   `failed_count`, show "X tasks failed — Retry & Resume" button that
   calls `?retry_failed=true`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] LINK-124 queue can be unblocked by clicking Retry & Resume in UI.
- [ ] All 7 failed tasks re-run cleanly to completion (verified by
      monitoring queue events post-resume).
- [ ] `test_resume_with_all_failed_returns_409_with_retry_hint` passes.
- [ ] `test_reset_failed_tasks_endpoint_marks_pending_and_keeps_completed`
      passes.
- [ ] `test_retry_failed_resume_flow` integration test passes
      end-to-end.

## Lineage

Discovered by debugger agent during LINK-124 deep-dive (RC3). This is
the user-facing unblock. Validate by unblocking the real LINK-124 queue
as part of QA.

items.title: S2 — Make circuit-breaker a terminal state transition (stop 60s event spam)
items.description:
## Bug

When `auto_resume_attempts > _AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, three code paths
(`_recovery_tick_once:764`, `resume_queue:2357`, `_fire_auto_resume:2730`)
set `queue.pause_reason='manual'` but **leave `queue.status` as
WAITING_RESET**. The 60s recovery tick predicate is:

```python
if queue.status != QueueStatus.WAITING_RESET: continue   # line 750
if queue.reset_time > lookahead: continue
if qid in self._resume_handles: continue
if queue.auto_resume_attempts > MAX:
    queue.pause_reason = "manual"
    self._persist_async(queue, "auto_resume_circuit_breaker_tripped", ...)
    continue                                              # never exits the queue from the loop
```

Same queue re-matches on the next tick. Forever. Evidence: LINK-124 has
20+ `auto_resume_circuit_breaker_tripped` events at exact 60s cadence.

## Scope

When the breaker trips:
- Transition `WAITING_RESET → PAUSED` (paired with
  `pause_reason='manual_circuit_breaker'`) via `transition_state`.
- Emit `auto_resume_circuit_breaker_tripped` event EXACTLY ONCE
  (idempotent — guarded on `pause_reason` already being the breaker value).
- Cancel any live `_resume_handles[qid]` timer.
- Tick predicate at 750 stops matching because status is now PAUSED.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After breaker trips, queue.status is `PAUSED` in both memory + DB.
- [ ] Subsequent tick iterations do NOT re-emit the event.
- [ ] Resume from the breaker-tripped state requires user action (manual
      resume), per the runbook.
- [ ] New unit test: `test_circuit_breaker_trip_is_terminal` — simulates
      4 ticks, asserts EXACTLY ONE breaker event and final status=PAUSED.

## Lineage

Discovered by debugger + code-reviewer agents during LINK-124 deep-dive
(RC1).

items.title: S1 — Persist auto_resume_attempts to DB (and fix increment ordering)
items.description:
## Bug

`auto_resume_attempts` is a dataclass field that lives only in memory.
There is no column for it in `AutoPilotQueueRecord`. On every backend
restart, `_record_to_queue` rebuilds the queue with `auto_resume_attempts=0`
(dataclass default). Result: the `_AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` circuit
breaker is **silently defeated** any time the backend restarts during a
waiting_reset.

Compounding: in `resume_queue` the counter is incremented BEFORE the
cap check (line 2354 → 2357). The 4th tick increments to 4, then the
cap check at 2357 catches it — but the increment already happened. The
tick-loop fast path at line 758 also reads `attempts > MAX` after the
increment.

## Scope

1. Add `autoResumeAttempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` to
   `AutoPilotQueueRecord` (SQLAlchemy + Prisma mirror + migration).
2. `save_queue` writes it. `_record_to_queue` reads it.
3. Move the increment in `resume_queue` to AFTER the cap check. Same for
   `_fire_auto_resume`.
4. Add `recent_failures` and `_appended_count` persistence consideration
   (decide: persist or accept they reset on restart).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration created and applied to dev.db (and a backfill safeguard
      for existing rows — default 0).
- [ ] `save_queue → fresh service → rehydrate → queue.auto_resume_attempts
      equals persisted value` — new unit test.
- [ ] Cap check fires AFTER increment, so increment never exceeds the cap.
- [ ] No regression on existing `test_auto_resume_scheduler.py` cases.

## Lineage

Discovered by debugger agent during LINK-124 deep-dive (RC2).

items.title: AutoPilot Resume / Recovery Reliability — structural refactor
items.description:
## Why

Queue `1d0304d2-fa15-4fd0-ad32-529f19dae96f` (feature LINK-124, sibling
project LinkedInJobHunterProduction) hit token exhaustion mid-run, never
recovered, and now leaks a `auto_resume_circuit_breaker_tripped` event
every 60 seconds. Three independent agent investigations (general-purpose
data-flow map, debugger root-cause graph, code-reviewer structural review)
converged on the same six root causes. This FEATURE delivers the
structural refactor; LINK-124 is unblocked as a side effect of S3.

## Six confirmed root causes

- **RC1** Circuit-breaker trip mutates `pause_reason='manual'` but leaves
  `queue.status=WAITING_RESET`. Tick loop predicate matches forever; event
  re-fires every 60 s. `autopilot_queue_service.py:764-768`.
- **RC2** `auto_resume_attempts` has no DB column. Resets to 0 on every
  backend restart, defeating the circuit breaker entirely. Plus: counter is
  incremented BEFORE the cap check, so it can pass the threshold during a
  single resume attempt. `autopilot_repository.py:save_queue` (column absent)
  and `autopilot_queue_service.py:2354`.
- **RC3** `_find_next_pending` only matches `TaskStatus.PENDING`. When all
  remaining tasks are `FAILED` (7 of 22 on LINK-124), resume returns False
  → API 400. Failed tasks have no retry path through the Resume button.
  `autopilot_queue_service.py:2373-2394`.
- **RC4** `detect_exhaustion_from_session` scans last 4 KB of CLI output.
  Claude CLI dumps 40-200 KB of tool output; token-exhaustion marker
  scrolls out of window. Systemic fallback uses 60s window — tasks run
  2-15 min, so 3 failures in 60s is mathematically impossible.
  `exhaustion_detector.py:432-475` + `autopilot_queue_service.py:347`.
- **RC5** `clear_recovery_state` is a 1-line no-op
  (`self._recovered_queue_ids.discard(qid)`). Doesn't touch DB, doesn't
  cancel timers, doesn't remove from `_zombie_queue_ids` or `_queues`.
  Returns `{ok:true}` while doing nothing. `autopilot_queue_service.py:889-891`.
- **RC6** `recovery-status` hard-codes `"state": "running"` for zombies and
  `"state": "waiting_reset"` for auto-resume-pending, ignoring the actual
  DB row. Three sources of truth for one field. `api/execution.py:1090,1102`.

## Load-bearing assumption that's broken

> "If a queue is in `self._queues`, it's healthy. If a transition function
>  gets called, it succeeds."

Wrong because 16 sites mutate `queue.status = X` directly bypassing
`transition_state()`. Callers wrap `IllegalStateTransitionError` in
`try/except: log+continue`. Memory and DB drift silently. DB is supposed
to be source of truth but is rarely consulted post-startup.

## Out of scope (separate features)

- Multi-project queue isolation (`_active_queue_id` is global today).
- Per-task force-retry UI flow on the AutoPilot panel.
- Webhook-driven resume (e.g. github push triggers resume of a paused
  queue).

## Deliverables (six child STORIES)

S1 → S6 in dependency order. Each STORY has its own acceptance gates:
unit tests for the RC's deterministic repro recipe, code-reviewer gate,
security-auditor gate (where applicable), integration test of the full
"crash → restart → resume → success" flow.

LINK-124 unblock is validated as the end-to-end regression for S3.

items.title: [REGRESSION] Credit-exhaustion detector misses silent claude CLI exit (LINK-124 cascade)
items.description:
## Repro (real, 2026-05-10)

LinkedInJobHunter project, queue 1d0304d2 (LINK-124 F28). 8 tasks succeeded, then 14 consecutive failures all 'Process exited with code 1' in <2 min. ZERO TOKEN_EXHAUSTION_DETECTED events emitted. Eli's credits exhausted mid-run.

## Why detector missed

`detect_exhaustion_from_session()` (utils/exhaustion_detector.py:553) reads `session.output[-80:]` + `session.error`. When claude CLI exits silently with code 1 due to Anthropic API credit exhaustion, the error happens INSIDE the claude binary's HTTP client — NOT printed to its stdout/stderr that we capture.

Result: detector sees only 'Process exited with code 1' → returns None → queue treats each as normal failure → CONTINUE_MARK_FAILED → next task → fails same way → loop until queue ends.

## Fix proposal

Add heuristic detector layer in autopilot_queue_service.py:
- Track per-queue rolling counter of consecutive failures with identical error text
- Threshold: N=3 consecutive failures within T=60s, all matching `Process exited with code` → assume systemic failure (likely credits/auth) → transition queue to PAUSED with reason='suspected_credit_exhaustion', emit TOKEN_EXHAUSTION_DETECTED with category='unknown_systemic'
- Schedule auto-resume after 30 min (assume credits back)
- Circuit breaker: if pause→resume cycle 2x with same systemic pattern → escalate to PAUSED/manual

## Affected

- backend/services/autopilot_queue_service.py (run_queue failure branch line 1022+)
- New helper: detect_systemic_failure(queue, recent_failures) -> bool
- New test: backend/tests/test_systemic_credit_detection.py

## Acceptance

- 3 consecutive 'Process exited with code 1' within 60s → queue paused (not 14 cascade)
- Existing exhaustion detection still wins when stdout/stderr has Anthropic patterns
- Recovery via existing reset+resume flow
- Bible Rule 25 regression: chaos suite + existing detector tests still green

## Workaround applied (2026-05-10)

LINK-124 queue manually recovered via /pause + 14× /task/{order}/reset. State now: paused, 8/22 idx=8, 14 pending. User can Resume when credits return.

items.title: [REGRESSION] Feature page Auto Pilot selection: count wrong + modal pulls unrelated stories + no per-row deselect
items.description:
## Repro (real)

Project LinkedInJobHunter, feature LINK-124 (F28 Dashboard V4).

1. Open `/codeboard/feature/<LINK-124-id>`
2. Click 'Select (and all children)' on EPIC LINK-135 (Insights Dashboard)

5. Click small `Auto Pilot (25)` → modal opens

7. Modal lists tasks from LINK-1049 (unrelated story) + its children LINK-1050/1051/1052
8. No per-row checkbox to deselect — only Select All Tasks / Deselect All bulk

## Root cause (3 separate gaps)

**Gap A — Top-right button count** `frontend/app/codeboard/feature/[id]/page.tsx:203`
- `executableTasks` collects ALL executables from tree
- Has no access to selection state owned by `HierarchyTreeSection`

**Gap B — Modal ignores tree selection** `frontend/components/codeboard/FeatureExecutionPanel.tsx:85,95-100,149`
- Receives `feature` + `allIssues`, NOT `selectedIds`
- Refetches `useIssueDescendants(feature.id)` → pulls ALL descendants of feature
- On open: `setSelectedIds(new Set(executableItems.map(i => i.id)))` reseeds from full set

**Gap C — No per-row checkbox** `FeatureExecutionPanel.tsx:240+,416-420`

- Modal opens with tree-selected tasks pre-checked AND filters to subtree of selection (no LINK-1049 if not selected)
- Per-row checkbox lets user deselect individual tasks before starting

- Bible Rule 25 full regression — no break to CB-1955 multi-select, CB-2018 per-card select, CB-2737 retry, CB-2775 resume UX

## Approach (per Eli 2026-05-10)

1. File this BUG (Rule 28)
2. Deep architecture audit BEFORE code (callers, deps, tests, risk)
3. Then propose precise fix → Eli approves → implement
4. NO rushed fix

items.title: [CB-2784 audit follow-up M-1] MEDIUM: /api/search/{project_id}/stats (get_index_stats) still echoes str(e) on exception — same disclosure shape CB-2784 closed for embed_all_issues
items.description:
**Severity:** MEDIUM — found by security-auditor on the CB-2784 fix (2026-05-10). Same threat model as CB-2784 but on the sibling endpoint `/api/search/{project_id}/stats`.

## Disclosure

`backend/api/search.py:329-335` (`get_index_stats`) still returns:

```python
except Exception as e:
    return {
        "project_id": project_id,
        "indexed_count": 0,
        "status": "error",
        "error": str(e),
    }
```

Token-holding callers are in scope by design (`InternalAuthDep` + 30/min cap), but on a CB-2732 bypass path an attacker who lands one successful `/stats` call learns the upstream error class — same CB-2784 leak shape.

## Fix

Mirror CB-2784: redact the response `error` field to a generic `stats_failed` token; keep `project_id` (path param). Route detail to `logger.exception` only.

Suggested form:

```python
except Exception:
    logger.exception("stats_failed", extra={"project_id": project_id})
    return {
        "project_id": project_id,
        "indexed_count": 0,
        "status": "error",
        "error": "stats_failed",
    }
```

## Test parity

Add a behavioural test (mirror `test_cb2784_embed_all_redaction.py`) asserting `body['error']` does not contain `str(e)`-derived substrings on a synthetic `rag.get_collection(...)` failure.

_Filed by Jonny during CB-2784 implementation pass._
items.implementationSummary:
CB-2787 addressed a MEDIUM-severity information disclosure vulnerability in the `/api/search/{project_id}/stats` (`get_index_stats`) endpoint. The exception handler was echoing `str(e)` directly into the JSON response body, leaking internal error details (stack traces, SQL errors, filesystem paths, ChromaDB internals) to token-holding callers and potentially to attackers who bypassed CB-2732 rate limits.

The fix mirrors the CB-2784 pattern: the `except Exception as e:` clause was changed to `except Exception:` (no bound name), the response `error` field was replaced with the static literal `'stats_failed'`, and full exception details are now routed exclusively to `logger.exception('stats_failed', extra={'project_id': project_id})` for server-side observability without client exposure.

A parity test file (`test_cb2787_stats_redaction.py`) was added mirroring CB-2784's test structure. It includes a behavioral assertion that 13 leak-shaped substrings (SQL, filesystem, ChromaDB, secret patterns) are absent from the response `error` field on synthetic `rag.get_collection()` failures, plus an AST source-pin test that walks `get_index_stats` and blocks any `Return` inside an `ExceptHandler` that references the bound exception name or `str(<name>)`. All 5 tests (2 new + 3 CB-2784 regression) pass. CB-2787 was marked `COMPLETED_WAITING_QA` in CodeBoard.

items.title: [CB-2732 audit follow-up I-5] MEDIUM: /api/search/* gates are auth-only, not project-scoped — token-holder can still walk any project_id (CB-2117-style follow-up)
items.description:
**Severity:** MEDIUM — flagged by security-auditor during the CB-2732 audit pass (2026-05-09). Out of CB-2732 stated scope (gate is auth-only by design, matching CB-2666 / CB-2667 perimeter posture); filed as a follow-up for the multi-tenant story.

## Issue

`InternalAuthDep` checks `X-Internal-Token` presence + correctness. It does NOT verify the caller-supplied `project_id` is one the caller is authorised to read or mutate. After CB-2732 a token-holding caller can still:

- `GET /api/search/<any-cuid>?q=...` and learn semantic-search   results for any project the operator owns
- `POST /api/search/<any-cuid>/embed-all` and confirm a   guessed CUID by the non-zero `embedded` count, while pinning   a worker for the duration of the fan-out
- `DELETE /api/search/<any-cuid>/embed/<any-iid>` and destroy   embeddings on a project they do not own

The runbook docstring at the top of `search.py` claims `embed-all` "confirms a guessed CUID by non-zero `embedded` count" — that claim still holds AFTER the gate for any token-holding client. The gate closes the **anonymous** perimeter; project-scoped authorisation is a separate layer.

## Fix recommendation

Same shape as CB-2117 (projectId IDOR guard on issue endpoints): add a project-scope check that resolves the caller to a Project row and verifies the supplied `project_id` matches a project the caller owns. The check runs INSIDE the route body or as a second `Depends(...)` after `InternalAuthDep`.

Note: the current deploy model is single-tenant (Eli is the operator and owns every project), so this is not exploitable today. The follow-up exists for when the perimeter expands (team / multi-tenant deploy).

## Test parity

After the fix lands, extend `TestSearchSiblingEndpointsPerimeter` (or add a sibling class) covering: token valid + project_id owned by caller → 200; token valid + project_id owned by another caller → 403.

## Threat-model linkage

CB-2117 (issue-endpoint projectId IDOR) → CB-2666 (project list gate) → CB-2667 (`/stats` gate) → CB-2732 (sibling search gates) → THIS (project-scoped authorisation on the search router for multi-tenant). Closing this finishes the authorisation perimeter the gate-only fixes built on.

_Filed by Jonny during CB-2732 implementation pass._

items.title: [CB-2732 audit follow-up L-3] LOW: rag_service.embed_issue / delete_issue_embedding use print() for errors — convert to logger.exception
items.description:
**Severity:** LOW — discovered by security-auditor on the CB-2732 fix (2026-05-09). Pre-existing pattern, but the new CB-2732 write endpoints (`POST /embed/{iid}`, `POST /embed-all`, `DELETE /embed/{iid}`) are now the user-facing entry points that drive these prints under attacker control.

## Issue

`backend/services/rag_service.py:902, :913` use:

```python
print(f"Error embedding issue: {e}")
```

Raw exception text → stdout, captured by any log shipper without the redaction logic the structured logger provides. Violates project convention (`CLAUDE.md`): "Logging: Python `logging` module (no print statements)."

## Fix

Convert `print(...)` → `logger.exception(...)` so any future log-redaction layer (Bearer/sk-/api_key= patterns the AutoPilot audit log already strips) catches accidental token spillage in the exception message.

Sweep the entire `rag_service.py` module for other `print()` instances while in there.

_Filed by Jonny during CB-2732 implementation pass._

items.title: [CB-2732 audit follow-up L-2] LOW: embed_all_issues errors[] leaks raw exception strings — redact str(e) to a generic token
items.description:
**Severity:** LOW — discovered by security-auditor on the CB-2732 fix (2026-05-09). Residual disclosure on bypass paths.

## Disclosure

`backend/api/search.py:276-279` and `:286` (`embed_all_issues`) return up to 10 entries in `errors[]` of the form:

```python
errors.append(f"Error embedding {issue.key}: {str(e)}")
```

If `e` carries a SQL error string, ChromaDB internal path, or HTTP-level chromadb error, the response body leaks more than the issue key. Token-holding callers are in-scope by design, but on a future bypass path (proxy-collapse / multi-worker scenario from CB-2732 audit M-3), an attacker who lands one successful `embed-all` call learns the project's issue keys via `errors[]` even when the bucket is otherwise capped.

## Fix

Redact `str(e)` to a generic `"embed_failed"` token; keep `issue.key` (caller already supplied it via `(project_id, issue_id)` in legitimate use). Mirror the redaction pattern the AutoPilot audit log uses (`Bearer/sk-/api_key=` strip).

Suggested form:

```python
except Exception as e:
    failed += 1
    errors.append(f"{issue.key}: embed_failed")
    logger.exception("embed_failed", extra={"issue_key": issue.key})
```

## Test parity

Add a regression test asserting `errors[]` entries do not contain `str(e)`-derived substrings (e.g. SQL error patterns, filesystem paths) on a synthetic embed failure.

_Filed by Jonny during CB-2732 implementation pass._
items.implementationSummary:
CB-2784 addressed a LOW-severity security finding where `embed_all_issues` in `backend/api/search.py` was leaking raw exception strings (potentially containing SQL errors, filesystem paths, or ChromaDB internals) into the `errors[]` array of API responses. The fix redacts `str(e)` to the generic token `embed_failed`, preserving only `issue.key` in the response while routing full exception detail to a structured logger via `logger.exception()` with `extra={"issue_key": ..., "project_id": ...}`.

A dedicated regression test file `backend/tests/test_cb2784_embed_all_redaction.py` was created with 3 tests: (1) behavioural verification that exception-branch errors contain no SQL/FS-path/ChromaDB/secret-shaped substrings, (2) behavioural verification of the non-raise branch, and (3) an AST-level source pin asserting the `errors.append(...)` call inside `except` blocks does not reference the bound exception name. All 3 new tests passed, and 34/34 CB-2732 sibling perimeter/invariant tests confirmed no regression.

An out-of-scope finding was identified during audit: `get_index_stats` at `search.py:334` still echoes `str(e)`, which was filed as new issue CB-2787 (MEDIUM). A `MIGRATION_NOTES.md` entry documents the response-shape change for API consumers. The CodeBoard issue was transitioned to `COMPLETED_WAITING_QA` and a helper script was saved under `scripts/codeboard/` per project Rule 29.

items.title: [CB-2732 audit follow-up L-1] LOW: search.py file-level invariant test — every router-decorated handler must carry InternalAuthDep + @limiter.limit
items.description:
**Severity:** LOW — discovered by security-auditor on the CB-2732 fix (2026-05-09).

## Gap

`backend/tests/test_security.py::TestSearchSiblingEndpointsPerimeter::test_handler_carries_internal_auth_dep` AST-pins the FIVE named CB-2732 handlers + the `/stats` handler from CB-2667. The parametrize list `_SEARCH_SIBLING_ENDPOINTS` is hard-coded, so if a future ticket adds a SIXTH endpoint to `backend/api/search.py` (e.g. `POST /{project_id}/reindex-since`) and forgets the gate, no test fails.

## Fix

Add a separate file-level invariant test that walks every `FunctionDef` / `AsyncFunctionDef` in `search.py` decorated by `@router.<verb>(...)` and asserts each one:

1. carries `dependencies=[...]` with `InternalAuthDep` in the kwarg
2. carries a `@limiter.limit(...)` decorator with a known cap
3. has `@router.<verb>` ABOVE `@limiter.limit` in source (decorator-order invariant from CB-2732 sec audit M-1)

This generalises the per-handler AST check to a per-file invariant. Same pattern should arguably apply to `backend/api/projects.py` (CB-2666 perimeter) — extend the test or extract a helper if so.

## Threat-model linkage

CB-2732 closed the perimeter on the FIVE current sibling endpoints. This follow-up makes the closure structural — a file-level invariant a new endpoint cannot bypass without deliberately defeating the test.

_Filed by Jonny during CB-2732 implementation pass._
items.implementationSummary:
CB-2783 implements a file-level AST invariant test for `backend/api/search.py` that generalises the per-handler checks introduced in CB-2732. Instead of a hard-coded parametrize list of named handlers, a new module-level helper `_collect_router_handlers(file_path)` walks every `FunctionDef`/`AsyncFunctionDef` in any target file and returns one record per `@router.<verb>(...)`-decorated function. This means any future endpoint added to `search.py` is automatically covered without a test update.

A new test class `TestSearchPyFileLevelInvariant` adds four tests: (1) a sanity floor asserting at least 6 handlers exist, (2) every handler carries `InternalAuthDep` in its `dependencies=[...]` kwarg, (3) every handler carries a `@limiter.limit(...)` decorator, and (4) `@router.<verb>` appears above `@limiter.limit` in source order (the decorator-order invariant from CB-2732 M-1). All four were mutation-tested against bad shapes (missing dep, missing limiter, inverted decorators, non-literal limit) and every violation was caught correctly.

No production code was modified. The extension to `api/projects.py` was intentionally deferred: `initialize_sequence` carries `InternalAuthDep` but lacks `@limiter.limit`, and resolving that requires a product decision on write-cap vs explicit exemption. The helper is file-agnostic, so the extension is a one-line parametrize once that decision is made. Full regression run: 1115 PASS + 3 pre-existing failures confirmed unrelated via `git stash` baseline. Both code-reviewer and security-auditor audit gates returned SHIP with no blockers.

items.title: [REGRESSION] Resume no-ops on CB-2038 — failed tasks at end + Resume/Retry UX broken
items.description:
## Repro

CB-2038 queue: 16 completed + 2 failed (CB-2731, CB-2732 — credit exhaustion). current_index=18/18.

1. Press Resume on AutoPilotFloatingBar → no-op (queue advances to idx 18, no task there)
2. Press Retry on failed task → broken (no UI response)
3. Recovery banner appears on left (duplicate of existing right floating bar)

## Root cause

Two gaps:
1. **`resume_queue()` advances `current_index` linearly.** When idx is past last task and pending tasks exist (because some failed earlier), it doesn't rewind to first pending. Hits end-of-queue, marks done, no-op.
2. **Retry-failed UX is split from Resume.** User must (a) reset each failed task individually, (b) then resume. Two-click flow not discoverable. UI conflates the two.

Bonus: AutoPilotRecoveryBanner (CB-2751 added) duplicates AutoPilotFloatingBar's data — both render for paused queues.

## Fix scope (7 tasks)

1. Audit `/queue/{id}/task/{order}/reset` endpoint — does it accept paused queue + failed task?
2. Wire Retry-Failed button on AutoPilotFloatingBar (per-failed-task + bulk)
3. Backend: `resume_queue()` rewinds to first pending when idx past last
4. Frontend: Resume button label = "Retry failed & Resume" when failed tasks exist
5. Regression pytest + Chrome QA on real CB-2038
6. Remove duplicate AutoPilotRecoveryBanner mount from service-monitor.tsx
7. Roll back CB-2746/2747-2755 mess (DELETED, link this BUG)

## Acceptance

- CB-2038 Resume after retry advances queue + runs CB-2731 + CB-2732
- One floating UI element (AutoPilotFloatingBar) — no duplicate banner
- Bible Rule 25 full regression green
- Eli does Chrome QA personally → DONE

## Linked

- Regresses: CB-1951 (parent feature)
- Affects: CB-2038 (stuck queue)
- Supersedes scope: CB-2746 (parallel feature, DELETED)

items.title: [BUG] AutoPilotStatusBadge className filter drops Tailwind color classes

items.title: [BUG] POST wait-for-reset doesn't set queue status to WAITING_RESET — badge stays amber
items.description:
## Summary

After calling `POST /api/execute/queue/{id}/wait-for-reset`, the queue's in-memory `status` remains `PAUSED` instead of transitioning to `WAITING_RESET`.

The status badge on the FloatingBar remains amber ('Paused') instead of changing to blue ('Waiting Reset').

## Root Cause

`autopilot_queue_service.wait_for_reset()` calls `_schedule_auto_resume()` which only arms an asyncio timer WITHOUT updating `queue.status = QueueStatus.WAITING_RESET`.

Contrast with the token-exhaustion path in `run_queue()` (line ~1066) which DOES set `queue.status = QueueStatus.WAITING_RESET` before scheduling the timer.

## Fix

In `wait_for_reset()` (autopilot_queue_service.py line ~2467), add:
```python
queue.status = QueueStatus.WAITING_RESET
queue.pause_reason = 'token_exhaustion'
queue.reset_time = target
```
before calling `_schedule_auto_resume(queue_id, target)`.

## Impact

- Status badge shows wrong color (amber instead of blue)
- Countdown timer in FloatingBar is not shown
- Recovery-status endpoint's `_suggested_action` returns 'resume' instead of 'wait'
- Users see ambiguous state

## Evidence

- After wait-for-reset: badge text='Paused', class contains `bg-amber-900/40` (not `bg-blue-900/40`)
- Queue API returns `status=paused reason=undefined` after wait-for-reset
- Expected: `status=waiting_reset reason=token_exhaustion`
- Verified in CB-2754 QA regression

items.title: [BUG] recovery-status returns stale response — CB-2750 recoverable/zombie fields missing
items.description:
## Summary

GET /api/execute/queue/recovery-status returns only the old CB-1951 format:
```json
{"recovered_count": 0, "queues": []}
```

The CB-2750 enriched fields (`recoverable[]`, `zombie[]`, `auto_resume_pending[]`) are MISSING.

## Impact

AutoPilotRecoveryBanner.tsx reads `recoverable[]` and `zombie[]` arrays from this endpoint. Without them, the banner NEVER renders any crash/waiting/zombie state. All recovery UI is invisible to users.

## Root Cause

Backend process started at 12:41PM. CB-2750 code deployed at 17:58PM. Without a backend restart, the old code is in memory. The .pyc file at 17:59 confirms module recompiled but not reloaded.

## Fix

Restart the backend (uvicorn process) to load latest execution.py. The code is correct on disk — only the running process has stale in-memory code.

## Evidence

- `curl http://localhost:8401/api/execute/queue/recovery-status` → `{"recovered_count":0,"queues":[]}`
- Expected: `{"recovered_count":0,"queues":[],"recoverable":[],"zombie":[],"auto_resume_pending":[]}`
- Backend PID 7888 started 12:41PM; execution.py modified 17:58PM
- Discovered during CB-2754 Chrome QA regression

items.title: [CB-2753 sec-audit HIGH] Unredacted subprocess error leaks via recovery-status + SSE (last_error / task.error / failureReason)
items.description:

items.title: [CB-2753 review HIGH] recoveryGeneration column lacks server_default — Base.metadata.create_all on fresh DB allows NULL inserts
items.description:
FILE: backend/models/autopilot.py:137 + frontend/prisma/schema.prisma:492

FINDING: SQLAlchemy column declared as:
  `recoveryGeneration = Column(Integer, nullable=False, default=0)`
The `default=0` is a Python-side default — applied at INSERT time by the ORM. If `Base.metadata.create_all` is used to create a fresh DB (e.g. in tests, first-run dev setup), the emitted DDL is `INTEGER NOT NULL` WITHOUT a server-side DEFAULT. The migration script DOES use `INTEGER DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL`, so production DBs after migration are fine, but raw-SQL inserts or tests that use the SQLAlchemy schema can violate the NOT NULL constraint.

FIX: Add `server_default='0'` to the SQLAlchemy column declaration so DDL emitted by `Base.metadata.create_all` matches the production migration:
  `recoveryGeneration = Column(Integer, nullable=False, default=0, server_default='0')`

PRIORITY: HIGH — drift between DDL paths is exactly the production-migration risk that focus area #6 calls out.

items.title: [CB-2753 review HIGH] _persist re-raise from _finalize_queue can leak unhandled exception out of run_queue task
items.description:
FILE: backend/services/autopilot_queue_service.py:1098, 1895

FINDING: Per the CB-2748 G3 fix, `_persist()` now re-raises OperationalError (disk_full / db_locked) and other exceptions instead of swallowing them. However, `_finalize_queue()` is called at line 1098 — OUTSIDE the run_queue try/except block (which ends at line 1095). The `_persist(queue, 'finalized', ...)` call at line 1895 inside `_finalize_queue` will therefore propagate any OperationalError uncaught out of the asyncio Task.

CONSEQUENCE: asyncio logs 'Task exception was never retrieved' to stderr, the tracked task callbacks (clear `_launching`, etc.) may fire late, and the queue lifecycle finalization is partially incomplete (lines 1900-1909, including the audit log info, do not run).

Mitigating factor: `_active_queue_id` clear (line 1888) and `_cancel_auto_resume` (line 1891) DO run before the failing _persist at 1895, so in-memory state IS cleaned up. But the 'finalized' STATE_TRANSITION-equivalent audit event is lost, and the prune-old-queues call (line 1902) is skipped — a long-running backend with frequent disk-full scenarios could accumulate terminal queues in `_queues`.

FIX: Wrap the `_persist(queue, 'finalized', ...)` call in `_finalize_queue` in its own try/except that emits PERSIST_FAILED via `emit_persist_failed_event` (best-effort) and continues with the prune step. Alternatively, move the _finalize_queue call INSIDE the run_queue try/except.

PRIORITY: HIGH — observable as accumulated terminal queues + asyncio noise on disk_full scenarios.

items.title: [CB-2753 review HIGH] Frontend hard-codes http://localhost:8401 — breaks Docker/non-localhost deployments
items.description:
FILE: frontend/components/codeboard/AutoPilotRecoveryBanner.tsx:47, 433

FINDING: Two hard-coded URLs:
  - `const BACKEND_API = 'http://localhost:8401/api/execute';`
  - `const BACKEND_EVENTS_URL = 'http://localhost:8401/api/execute/queue/events';`

The rest of the codebase uses fetch() to relative '/api/...' paths or relies on Next.js proxy. The hard-coded host breaks any deployment where the backend is not on localhost: docker-compose (different hostname), production reverse-proxy, remote dev preview.

Option (a) is the convention used elsewhere in the codebase (verify with `grep -r 'fetch("/api' frontend/`).

PRIORITY: HIGH — feature is unusable in any non-localhost deployment, including the project's own docker-compose setup.

items.title: [CB-2753 review HIGH] auto_resume_attempts double-incremented when timer + recovery tick race
items.description:
FILE: backend/services/autopilot_queue_service.py (_recovery_tick_once line 698, _fire_auto_resume line 2446)

FINDING: Both the timer-driven `_fire_auto_resume()` and the tick-driven `_recovery_tick_once()` increment `queue.auto_resume_attempts` and check the circuit breaker, neither of them holds `_resume_locks[queue_id]` at that point. (The lock is only acquired inside `resume_queue()`.)

RACE WINDOW: timer fires, `_runner` finishes, removes itself from `_resume_handles[qid]` in its `finally` block. Before `_fire_auto_resume` can complete the post-resume bookkeeping, the next 60-s tick wakes up. Tick sees `qid not in self._resume_handles` (line 695), proceeds to increment `auto_resume_attempts` AGAIN, and tries to call `resume_queue` AGAIN.

CONSEQUENCE: Counter advances twice per real auto-resume attempt → circuit breaker trips ~half as fast as the documented 3 attempts. Worse, the second `resume_queue` call may succeed (queue is now WAITING_RESET, but tick checks QueueStatus.WAITING_RESET — actually wait, by the time the second call happens queue is RUNNING, so resume_queue returns False fast). Counter inflation is the main impact.

FIX: Acquire `self._resume_locks[queue_id]` in BOTH `_fire_auto_resume` and `_recovery_tick_once` Pass 1 BEFORE incrementing the counter. Or move the counter increment INSIDE the lock-protected section of `resume_queue()` (single source of truth).

PRIORITY: HIGH — defeats the documented circuit-breaker invariant; failure mode is silent and only visible by inspecting auto_resume_attempts.

items.title: [CB-2753 review HIGH] _CREDIT_SIGNALS too broad: 'credits' / 'billing' / 'your account has' false-positive triggers
items.description:
FILE: backend/utils/exhaustion_detector.py:151-160

FINDING: `_CREDIT_SIGNALS` includes very generic substrings:
  - 'credits' — matches 'credits to the contributors', 'BONUS_CREDITS', etc.
  - 'billing' — matches 'billing/invoice', 'billing@example.com', etc.
  - 'your account has' — matches countless non-billing messages.

CONSEQUENCE: A subprocess that prints any normal text containing these substrings (e.g. README content read by claude, git commit messages, comment snippets in source files) AND happens to also have a non-zero exit code, will be classified as 'credit_exhaustion' and pause the queue with NO_AUTO_RESUME.

FIX: Tighten to multi-word, billing-specific patterns:
  - 'credit balance is too low'   (already present — keep)
  - 'insufficient_quota'           (keep)
  - 'out of credits'               (replace 'credits')
  - 'billing issue'                (replace 'billing')
  - 'payment required'             (keep)
Drop the lone 'credits' / 'billing' / 'your account has' substrings.

PRIORITY: HIGH — same user-blocking impact as the x-api-key finding above.

items.title: [CB-2753 review HIGH] _AUTH_SIGNALS contains 'x-api-key' substring — false positive on header dumps
items.description:
FILE: backend/utils/exhaustion_detector.py:144

FINDING: The `_AUTH_SIGNALS` frozenset includes the literal string 'x-api-key'. Any subprocess output that echoes a request header — including verbose curl output, debug logging, retry attempts that print headers, or even URL-encoded documentation snippets that mention the header name — will trigger 'auth_failure' classification.

CONSEQUENCE: Queues hit a perfectly normal 5xx or transient error that happens to dump a request header to stdout will be paused as 'auth_failure', go into NO_AUTO_RESUME mode, and demand the user fix their (working) API key.

FIX: Drop 'x-api-key' from _AUTH_SIGNALS — rely on `_extract_http_status() == 401` + JSON error.type detection (already in place) instead. The header-name substring is too broad for a credential-failure signal.

PRIORITY: HIGH — false-positive auth_failure is user-blocking (requires manual resume + investigation) and the failure mode is silent.

items.title: [CB-2753 review CRITICAL] checkpoint() never called — lastCheckpointAt always NULL, recovery promise unfulfilled
items.description:
FILE: backend/services/autopilot_queue_service.py + backend/utils/autopilot_repository.py:445

FINDING: `checkpoint()` is defined and unit-tested but never called from production code. Verified via grep.

CONSEQUENCES:
  1. `AutoPilotQueueRecord.lastCheckpointAt` will always be NULL.
  2. `CHECKPOINT_WRITTEN` audit events will never be emitted.
  3. The design promise ('a crash between checkpoints means the queue can recover to the last checkpoint position without re-running already-completed tasks') is unfulfilled.

FIX: Call `await checkpoint(queue.id)` after every successful task completion — the natural site is in `_apply_success` (line ~1611) immediately after the task_completed _persist call.

PRIORITY: CRITICAL — feature stub ships in DB schema and repository code, with a documented behavior contract that is silently violated.

items.title: [CB-2753 review CRITICAL] transition_state() never called from production — state machine is unenforced
items.description:
FILE: backend/services/autopilot_queue_service.py (every state mutation site)
      backend/utils/autopilot_repository.py:371 (transition_state)

FINDING: `transition_state()` is defined as the 'only authorised way to change queue state' (per the docstring), with state-machine validation against `_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` and STATE_TRANSITION audit-log emission. But it is NEVER CALLED from autopilot_queue_service.py — only from tests.

Production code mutates `queue.status` directly, e.g.:
  - line 1019: `queue.status = QueueStatus.PAUSED`
  - line 1031: `queue.status = QueueStatus.WAITING_RESET`
  - line 1067: `queue.status = QueueStatus.RUNNING`
  - line 1095: `queue.status = QueueStatus.ABORTED`
  - line 1637: `queue.status = QueueStatus.ABORTED`
  - line 1864: `queue.status = QueueStatus.COMPLETED`
  - line 2243: `queue.status = QueueStatus.ABORTED`

CONSEQUENCES:
  1. The state-machine validation table (`_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` in models/autopilot.py) is dead code — illegal transitions can occur silently.
  2. STATE_TRANSITION audit events are NEVER emitted in production. The frontend SSE listener subscribes to them (AutoPilotRecoveryBanner.tsx line 439) but will never receive any.
  3. The `state` and `stateReason` columns added by E2 are populated by a side-channel (`save_queue` mirrors `status`/`pauseReason`) but the canonical transition path is unused.

FIX: Either (a) refactor every state mutation site to go through transition_state(), or (b) document explicitly that transition_state() is reserved for future use and remove the misleading 'only authorised way' docstring. Option (a) is the bible-mandated path because the whole point of the E2 overhaul was the state machine.

PRIORITY: CRITICAL — focus area #1 explicitly called out: 'Each one is a latent bug class.'

items.title: [CB-2753 review CRITICAL] set_subprocess_pid() never wired into production — zombie detection non-functional
items.description:
FILE: backend/services/autopilot_queue_service.py + backend/utils/autopilot_repository.py:482

FINDING: `set_subprocess_pid()` is defined and unit-tested in CB-2748, but is NEVER CALLED from the production code path (autopilot_queue_service.py). Verified via `grep -rn set_subprocess_pid backend/` — only test files reference it.

CONSEQUENCE: The G2 zombie-detection logic in `rehydrate_from_db` (line 488-512) looks for `task_rec.subprocessPid`, but no production code path ever populates that column. So in real deployments, `_check_pid_alive()` will never run against a real PID — every rehydrated RUNNING queue is treated as crash_recovery (dead PID branch). The whole ZOMBIE_DETECTED feature is dead code in production.

The chaos test (`test_cat4_zombie_detection_running_with_alive_pid`) passes because it manually inserts os.getpid() into the task row.

FIX: In `_execute_task` (autopilot_queue_service.py around line 1411), after the subprocess is spawned in terminal_service, capture its PID and call `await set_subprocess_pid(task_record.id, pid, queue_id=queue.id)`. Clear it (pid=None) when the task completes/fails (around lines 1611, 1653, 1679, 1702, 1723).

PRIORITY: CRITICAL — feature ships broken; ZOMBIE_DETECTED audit-log entries will never appear, monitoring/alerting that depends on them is silently dead.

items.title: Bulletproof AutoPilot — survive ANY interruption + complete work (supersedes CB-1951 scope)
items.description:
## Mission

Once AutoPilot starts, it MUST survive any interruption and complete the work.
No more "queue disappeared" / "stuck in failed" / "ghost running" moments.

## Failure modes to survive (all)

1. Backend graceful shutdown (SIGTERM)
2. Backend SIGKILL (force)
3. Backend OOM kill
4. Backend uncaught exception
5. OS reboot mid-task (power cut, kernel panic, scheduled restart)
6. Anthropic API token exhaustion / rate limit (429, 529)
7. Anthropic API auth/credit failure (401)
8. Network blip (ECONNREFUSED, timeout)
9. Disk full during DB write
10. Subprocess SIGKILL (claude CLI killed externally)
11. Frontend disconnect mid-flow (SSE drops)
12. Multiple concurrent resume calls (race)

For each: queue state must be **recoverable + resumable** with a single user action (Resume button) or auto-recovery on backend startup.

## Why this supersedes CB-1951

CB-1951 was scoped to "pause/resume + crash recovery" but in production has failed multiple times:
- CB-2671: empty key/title on rehydrate (fixed)
- CB-2671 follow-up: same bug in create-queue path (fixed)
- CB-2737/CB-2743/CB-2744/CB-2745: reset endpoint, current_index, in-memory-only lookups, get_or_load_queue (fixed)
- TODAY (2026-05-09): credit exhaustion → tasks marked failed (not WAITING_RESET) → queue zombie running with no live coroutine → invisible to recovery-status

Pattern: each fix solved the immediate symptom but never the systemic guarantee. This feature fixes the guarantee.

## High-level scope

- E1 Research + state-machine design (formal model — no code)
- E2 Persistence overhaul (atomic writes, journal mode, write-ahead log, crash-safe checkpoints)
- E3 Token/credit exhaustion detection (broad pattern matching, exit code + output)
- E4 Recovery scheduler (rehydrate ALL non-terminal queues; scan zombie running; auto-resume after token reset)
- E5 UI surface (banner for every recoverable state; status badges; retry per-task; force-recover)
- E6 Chaos test suite (kill -9 mid-task; OOM; disk full simulation; token exhaust simulation; SSE drop)
- E7 Audits (code-reviewer + security-auditor)
- E8 Chrome QA full regression (every banner state + recovery action)
- E9 Rollout (migration + 24h soak)

Sequencing: E1 → E2/E3/E4 (parallel) → E5 → E6 → E7 → E8 → E9.

## Bible compliance

- Rule 18: 4-gate audit mandatory
- Rule 22: never DONE except by Eli
- Rule 23: full plan before any code (THIS ticket)
- Rule 25: full chaos regression mandatory before CWQ — no whack-a-mole
- Rule 27: durable artifacts in docs/plans/
- Rule 29: scripts in backend/scripts/codeboard/

## Linked

- Supersedes scope of CB-1951 (CWQ — keeps as historical reference)
- Closes (operationally) CB-2671, CB-2737, CB-2743, CB-2744, CB-2745, CB-2683 (security follow-ups)
- Blocks CB-2384 confidence (workspace can't ship until autopilot is bulletproof)

items.title: [CB-2737 systemic fix] All 6 queue-mutating service methods use in-memory-only lookup; convert to get_or_load_queue
items.description:
**Research finding 2026-05-09 (per Eli's feedback on bug-fix workflow):**

CB-2743 fixed reset endpoint but the SAME bug class lives in 6 other queue-mutating methods in `backend/services/autopilot_queue_service.py`:

| Method | Line | User action affected |
|---|---|---|
| pause_queue | 1751 | Pause button on recovered queue |
| resume_queue | 1768 | **Resume button (active symptom for Eli)** |
| skip_current | 1873 | Skip current task |
| abort_queue | 1897 | Abort/Stop button |
| _record_to_queue downstream check | 1977 | Recovery rehydrate path |
| switch_model | 2092 | Model switcher |

All use `self._queues.get(queue_id)` which returns None for paused-only-in-DB queues. The defensive Part B self-heal in resume_queue is correct but never fires because the in-memory check trips first.

**Fix:**
1. Convert all 6 methods to async; replace `self._queues.get(queue_id)` with `await self.get_or_load_queue(queue_id)` (already exists from CB-2743)
2. Update API endpoints (execution.py) that call them — they're already async, just need to await
3. New regression test PER endpoint covering DB-only paused queue
4. Verify Eli's actual flow: queue 99ccf3aa is paused → POST resume → returns 200 → queue runs → CB-2729 completes

**Acceptance:**
- Manual curl resume on queue 99ccf3aa returns 200 + queue starts running
- Full Chrome regression in `/codeboard` UI: press Resume on banner → queue advances → tasks visible in floating bar
- All 877 existing tests pass + new tests for each endpoint on DB-only queue

Bible: Rule 22, 23, 25 (full regression mandatory), 28.

items.title: [CB-2737 fix] Reset endpoint must rewind current_index when failed tasks revert to pending — resume otherwise refuses with "no active task at 18/18"
items.description:
Eli pressed Resume on queue 99ccf3aa after CB-2743 fix flipped 4 failed tasks (orders 14-17) back to pending. Backend log:
```
WARNING - Queue 99ccf3aa-... resume refused — no active task at index 18/18
HTTP 400 — Cannot resume — queue is not paused or does not exist
```

Queue.current_index = 18 (one past last task), so resume_queue() refuses. The reset endpoint flipped task statuses but didn't rewind current_index.

**Fix:** in `services/autopilot_queue_service.py` (or the reset path) — after a task is reset to pending, set `queue.current_index = min(queue.current_index, lowest_pending_order)`. Persist via save_queue.

**Defense in depth (recommended):** resume_queue should also scan for any pending task, not blindly trust current_index. If found, set current_index to that order and proceed.

**Acceptance:**
- Reset task at order < current_index → current_index rewound to that order
- Resume on queue with pending tasks past current_index → still proceeds (defensive)
- Eli's resume on CB-2038 queue (99ccf3aa) succeeds and runs CB-2729-CB-2732
- New regression test

**Bible:** Rule 22, 23, 28. Same family.

items.title: [CB-2737 fix] Reset endpoint returns 404 for paused queues — get_queue is in-memory only, doesn't load from DB
items.description:
Reset endpoint at `backend/api/execution.py:1346` uses `autopilot_queue_service.get_queue(queue_id)` which only checks in-memory `_queues` dict. After backend restart, paused queues exist in DB (`AutoPilotQueueRecord` with status=paused) but are not auto-loaded until resume_queue is called. This makes the retry-task endpoint return 404 for any task in a paused queue — exactly the user-facing case.

**Fix:** Add helper `_get_or_load_queue(queue_id)` in `services/autopilot_queue_service.py` that:
1. Returns from in-memory `_queues` if present
2. Otherwise loads from DB via existing rehydrate machinery (`_record_to_queue`)
3. Caches in `_queues` after load

Update reset endpoint (and audit any sibling endpoints with the same pattern: pause, resume's pre-resume lookup, abort, switch_model) to use the helper.

**Acceptance:**
- POST /api/execute/queue/{id}/task/{order}/reset succeeds for queue that was rehydrated only in DB
- Eli can click 'Retry all failed' on CB-2038 queue and the 4 failed tasks (CB-2729-CB-2732) flip to pending
- Existing tests still green; new test covers DB-only-queue reset path

Bible: Rule 22, 23, 28.

Stop using failureReason="backend_crash_recovery" — reserve failed status for real execution errors. Acceptance: simulated crash + rehydrate → in-flight task is `pending`, not `failed`.

items.title: [CB-2671 related] AutoPilot rehydrate marks crash-interrupted tasks as failed instead of pending; no UI to retry/reset failed tasks
items.description:
**Symptom (Eli, 2026-05-09):**

When backend restarts mid-task, the rehydrate-from-DB path marks the in-flight task as `failed` with `failureReason='backend_crash_recovery'`. Per queue config `on_fail: CONTINUE_MARK_FAILED`, AutoPilot then skips those tasks on resume. They never run.

User has no UI to:
- Reset a failed task to pending (had to do it manually via SQL for CB-2217)
- Retry a single failed task
- See "FAILED" status anywhere in CodeBoard (status enum has no FAILED — only AutoPilotTaskRecord.status field)

**Why this is wrong:**
Backend restart is NOT a task failure. The task didn't error — it was interrupted by infrastructure. On resume, interrupted tasks should go back to `pending` and re-run, not be marked permanently failed.

**Live evidence:**
Queue `99ccf3aa-...` for CB-2038. Multiple tasks marked `failed/backend_crash_recovery` after credit-exhaustion + restart. Eli had to manually SQL-update CB-2217 to bring it back. Same will happen every backend restart.

**Fix scope:**

T1 (backend semantics fix) — `services/autopilot_queue_service.py:rehydrate_from_db`:
- Tasks that were `running` at crash time → reset to `pending` (NOT failed)
- Use a different status like `interrupted` if we want to track crash count separately, but treat as resumable
- `failureReason='backend_crash_recovery'` should stop being used for crash recovery; reserve `failed` for real execution errors

T2 (backfill existing wrong-state tasks) — script under `backend/scripts/backfill_crash_to_pending.py`:
- Find AutoPilotTaskRecord rows with status='failed' AND failureReason='backend_crash_recovery'
- Reset to status='pending', clear failureReason

T3 (UI retry button) — `frontend/components/codeboard/AutoPilotFloatingBar.tsx` (and IssueDetailModal/HierarchyTreeSection where task list shown):
- Per failed task: small "Retry" button that POSTs to a new endpoint `/api/execute/queue/{id}/task/{taskId}/reset` which flips the row back to pending
- Optional: bulk "Reset all crash-recovered failed → pending" button on AutoPilot bar

T4 (regression test) — assert simulated crash + rehydrate reclassifies running→pending, not failed.

T5 (audit) — code-reviewer + Chrome QA.

**Bible:** Rule 22, 23, 28. Same root-cause family as CB-2671 (autopilot rehydrate hygiene).

items.title: [CB-2667 sec audit follow-up H-1] HIGH: sibling /api/search/* endpoints share per-project_id disclosure / write-amplification shape
items.description:
**Severity:** HIGH — a partial fix on `/stats`
(CB-2667) leaves five sibling endpoints under `backend/api/search.py`
exposed to the SAME threat model that CB-2667 closed. Until these are
gated, the CB-2666 + CB-2667 perimeter is incomplete on any non-loopback
deploy.

**Discovery:** security-auditor pass on the CB-2667 fix
(2026-05-09). H-1 is filed here rather than rolled into CB-2667 to
keep the original ticket scope-pure (single endpoint per fix).

## Affected endpoints

| Method | Path | Disclosure / Amplification |
|---|---|---|
| GET    | `/api/search/{project_id}` | per-project semantic search results (issue content disclosure) |
| GET    | `/api/search/{project_id}/similar` | per-project similar-issue results (issue content disclosure) |
| POST   | `/api/search/{project_id}/embed/{issue_id}` | mutates arbitrary collection — DoS amplification + IDOR write |
| DELETE | `/api/search/{project_id}/embed/{issue_id}` | deletes arbitrary embeddings — destructive IDOR |
| POST   | `/api/search/{project_id}/embed-all` | iterates EVERY Issue with `projectId == X` and embeds them — server-side fan-out, validates guessed CUIDs by 200-with-`embedded>0` |

## Fix recommendation

Apply the SAME pattern CB-2666 / CB-2667 established:

```python
@router.get(
    "/{project_id}",
    dependencies=[InternalAuthDep],
)
@limiter.limit("30/minute")
async def search_issues(request: Request, ...):
    ...
```

The two write endpoints (`POST /embed*`, `DELETE /embed*`,
`POST /embed-all`) deserve a STRICTER cap (suggest 10/minute) — they
are DoS-amplifying, not just disclosure. `embed-all` in particular
walks every Issue row matching `projectId` and embeds each one
synchronously, so a single request can pin the worker for seconds
on a large project.

## Runbook update needed

`backend/docs/DOC_PIPELINE_RUNBOOK.md` §3 currently lists `/stats`
as the only gated search endpoint. After this fix lands, extend
the table to cover all six routes under `/api/search/*` and note
the stricter cap on the write endpoints.

## Test parity

Mirror the `TestSearchStatsEndpointPerimeter` class — one parametrized
class per endpoint (or one shared parametrized fixture covering the
endpoint + method matrix) covering: token unset, missing header,
valid header, wrong header, Origin spoof, AST-walk source-text pin.

## Reproduction (post CB-2667, pre this fix)

With `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN=""` (default loopback dev):

```bash
# All 5 still 200 — same as before CB-2667
curl -s 'http://localhost:8401/api/search/<any-cuid>?q=foo' | head -c 200
curl -s 'http://localhost:8401/api/search/<any-cuid>/similar?title=foo' | head -c 200
```

With token set:

```bash
# /stats now 401 (CB-2667 fix), but the 5 siblings still 200 — gap.
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'http://localhost:8401/api/search/<any-cuid>/stats'
# → 401
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'http://localhost:8401/api/search/<any-cuid>?q=foo'
# → 200 (this is the gap)
```

## Threat-model linkage

CB-2217 (anonymous `count[]`) → CB-2666 H-1 (project_id list, gated)
→ CB-2667 H-2 (`/stats` per-project count, gated) → THIS (`/search/*`
sibling endpoints, ungated). Closing this finishes the perimeter
the CB-2217 redaction was supposed to provide.

_Filed by security-auditor agent during CB-2667 audit pass._
items.implementationSummary:
CB-2732 applied the same `InternalAuthDep` + `@limiter.limit` perimeter pattern established by CB-2666/CB-2667 to all five sibling `/api/search/*` endpoints that were left unguarded. Read endpoints (`GET /{project_id}` and `GET /{project_id}/similar`) received a 30/minute cap, while the DoS-amplifying write endpoints (`POST /embed/{issue_id}`, `DELETE /embed/{issue_id}`, `POST /embed-all`) received a stricter 10/minute cap.
