items.title: Issue Correlation & Grouping
items.description:
Allow related issues to be linked beyond strict parent-child hierarchy.

Two primitives:
1. **Issue ↔ Issue typed relations** (m2m): RELATES_TO, DUPLICATES, BLOCKS, IS_BLOCKED_BY, CAUSED_BY, CAUSES, IS_DUPLICATED_BY. Wire up the existing-but-unused IssueLink table at `backend/models/issue.py:158-174`.
2. **Issue Groups**: named clusters of N issues with computed aggregate status (group "complete" when all members reach COMPLETED_WAITING_QA). New entity, mirrors QATaskIssueLink shape.

**Why now**: today the only relation between issues is `parentId` (single hierarchy). When two bugs share a root cause but aren't strict parent-child, the tree gets fudged. CB-1945 (cascade hardening umbrella) is the live example — currently parented as a fake hierarchy.

**Design backed by**:
- Code Review for AI Agents v4 (association object pattern, p. 197 — Primitive Obsession rule)
- UI/UX Design Principles for AI Agents (p. 7 — grouped flat list, NOT graph widget per Miller's Law)
- Web Application Security for AI Agents (p. 8 — enum validation, mass-assignment protection)
- Supabase PostgreSQL Best Practices (p. 8 — N+1 avoidance, FK indexes mandatory on cascade)
- api-designer agent contract draft (5 endpoint groups, full payload + error model)

**Scope**: see child Epics. Migrates CB-1945/CB-1946/CB-1954 fake umbrella to a real group at the end.

**Out of scope** (future features):
- Visual graph view of relation network
- AI-suggested groupings ("these N bugs look related")
- Cross-project relations

items.title: DELETE /relations: no test for legacy cross-project rows
items.description:
**Found by**: CB-1981 security audit (MEDIUM).

**Issue**: `delete_relation` in `backend/api/relations.py:725+` collapses wrong-owner attempts to 404 and notes its cross-project safety depends on the create-time same-project invariant. With legacy cross-project rows still possible (pre-CB-1980 / future migrations / direct DB write), the DELETE path is not exercised against that scenario.

**Acceptance**: Add a test that seeds a cross-project IssueLink directly, calls DELETE /api/issues/{a1}/relations/{legacy_id}, and confirms either (a) clean delete with both rows removed, or (b) defined error behavior — but NEVER an error envelope leaking project B issue ids in the message/details. Document whichever behavior we choose in relations.py docstring.

items.title: GET /relations missing projectId filter — leaks foreign-project rows
items.description:
**Found by**: CB-1981 security audit (HIGH→MEDIUM).

**Issue**: `list_relations` in `backend/api/relations.py:417` does NOT filter the IssueLink rows by `Issue.projectId`. If any legacy cross-project IssueLink row exists in the DB (pre-CB-1980 enforcement, future migration, direct DB write), it surfaces in `outbound`/`inbound` with foreign-project issue summaries embedded via `selectinload(IssueLink.fromIssue/toIssue)`.

**Compare**: `_has_cycle` (relations.py:201-208) already added the project filter as defense-in-depth (CB-1977). The GET path needs the same treatment.

**Fix**: JOIN to `Issue` and filter by `Issue.projectId == src.projectId` on both the outbound and inbound subqueries.

**Test**: Seed a cross-project IssueLink directly, GET /relations, assert the foreign-project row is NOT in either list.

items.title: H3 [HIGH]: DocSettings PATCH manually mutates updatedAt + relies on early-return for no-op
items.description:
**File**: `backend/api/doc_settings.py:65`

**Issue**: PATCH handler manually sets `row.updatedAt = datetime.utcnow()` only when `data` is non-empty. Model already has `onupdate=_utc_now`. Manual setting is redundant + fragile — if a future caller adds a side-effecting branch above the early return, SQLAlchemy `onupdate` would re-bump on flush even for no-op.

**Fix**: drop the manual `row.updatedAt = ...` line and rely exclusively on `onupdate`. Verify behavior with a test that PATCHes empty body and confirms `updatedAt` unchanged.

Source: code-reviewer CB-2068.

items.title: H1 [HIGH]: process_doc_retention sleeps 6h before first pass — boot-time misconfigs not surfaced
items.description:
**File**: `backend/app/main.py:204-222`

**Issue**: `process_doc_retention` calls `await asyncio.sleep(_RETENTION_INTERVAL_SECONDS)` BEFORE first pass. With retentionDays=1 (or any aggressive setting), user sees no purge for 6h.

**Fix**: schedule a fast follow-up pass ~60s after boot, then continue at 6h cadence. Log `[startup]` line on first execution.

Source: code-reviewer CB-2068.

items.title: M2 [MEDIUM]: apply_retention walks all distinct issueIds in single transaction without batching
items.description:
**File**: `backend/services/doc_settings_service.py:70-90`

**Issue**: With N issues × 2 queries each, retention pass holds long-running write transaction on SQLite. Whole API blocks during the pass on disk lock.

**Effect**: If issue count grows to 50k, retention freezes backend for the duration. Not exploitable cross-tenant (single-operator) but DoS surface.

**Fix**: Periodic commit-per-batch (e.g., commit every 100 issues) + asyncio.sleep(0) yield to event loop between batches.

**Severity**: MEDIUM — operational DoS at scale only.

Source: security-auditor CB-2091.
items.implementationSummary:
Implemented CB-2123 fix for the `apply_retention` function in `doc_settings_service.py` which previously held a single long-running SQLite write transaction across all distinct issue IDs during retention passes. The fix introduces a `_RETENTION_BATCH_SIZE = 100` module constant, commits and yields to the event loop (`await asyncio.sleep(0)`) after every 100 issues in phase 2, and also commits immediately after phase 1 (age delete) to release the write lock before phase 2 begins.

The docstring contract was updated to reflect that `apply_retention()` now commits internally and callers must NOT wrap it in `db.begin()`. A new test `test_apply_retention_batches_and_yields` was added that patches `_RETENTION_BATCH_SIZE` to 5, seeds 12 issues × 3 rows, and asserts correct purge count, ≥4 commits during the pass, and that `asyncio.sleep` was awaited at least once with delay 0.

Code-reviewer and security-auditor sub-agents were run in parallel. All medium/high findings from code review were applied (sleep monkeypatch hygiene, counter comment, loose assertion tightening, docstring warning). The security auditor found no CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM issues; one LOW finding was skipped per policy. Final test results: 14/14 doc_settings tests pass, 6/6 e3 regression tests pass, 790 pass in full suite with only 3 pre-existing unrelated failures.

items.title: M1 [MEDIUM]: apply_retention notin_(keep_ids) may hit SQLite variable limit on legacy SQLite
items.description:
**File**: `backend/services/doc_settings_service.py:76-89`

**Issue**: Per-issue retention cap builds `keep_ids` set (up to maxPerIssue=1000 elements) then passes to `delete().where(notin_(keep_ids))`. SQLAlchemy expands to `NOT IN (?, ?, ...)` parameter list. SQLite default `SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER` is 999 on legacy builds (3.32+ raises to 32766).

**Effect**: With maxPerIssue=1000 on legacy SQLite, DELETE throws `OperationalError: too many SQL variables`. The retention loop's outer except swallows it, so cap silently fails to apply for that issue.

**Fix options**:
1. Chunk the `notin_` set (delete in batches of 500)
2. Invert the predicate: query oldest_keep_executedAt, then `delete().where(executedAt < oldest_keep_executedAt)` — uses 1 parameter instead of N

**Severity**: MEDIUM — DoS-via-disk-exhaustion over time (cap silently fails so old rows accumulate).

Source: security-auditor CB-2091.

items.title: Add backend auth layer + project scoping to all /api/* endpoints (deferred from CB-2117)
items.description:

**Issue**: documentation API endpoints (and most other /api/* endpoints) have no per-request authorization. `_ensure_issue_exists` / `_load_feature_issue` look up by `Issue.id` only, with no projectId scoping and no caller identity check.

Currently acceptable for single-operator deployment but blocks multi-tenant use.

**Scope**: full repo audit + auth layer (likely OAuth/JWT or session cookie + per-project RBAC). Out of scope of CB-2038 Documentation Surface feature.

**Affected endpoints** (documentation feature alone):
- POST /api/issues/{id}/documentation/notes
- DELETE /api/issues/{id}/documentation/notes/{note_id}
- GET /api/issues/{id}/documentation
- GET /api/issues/{id}/documentation/latest
- GET /api/issues/{id}/documentation/notes
- GET /api/features/{id}/documentation
- POST /api/features/{id}/documentation/generate

**Priority**: HIGH for multi-tenant deployment, LOW for current single-operator use.

items.title: F5 [HIGH]: _run_git_subprocess has no cmd[0] == 'git' shape-check
items.description:
**File**: `backend/services/documentation_generator.py:701-709`

**Issue**: `_run_git_subprocess` calls `subprocess.run(cmd, ...)` with `shell=False` and a list argv (safe today). All current call sites pass `["git", ...]`. But the function has no shape-check — a future caller passing a single string or different binary would silently work.

Defense-in-depth gap. Not exploitable today.

**Fix**: Add at function entry:
```python
if not isinstance(cmd, list) or not cmd or cmd[0] != "git":
    raise ValueError(f"_run_git_subprocess requires list argv starting with 'git', got: {cmd!r}")
```

Source: code-reviewer (H3).

items.title: F4 [HIGH]: _capture_git_changes doesn't call validate_project_path — arbitrary-dir git execution
items.description:
**File**: `backend/services/documentation_generator.py:209-272`

**Issue**: `_capture_git_changes` consumes `project_path` from `TerminalSession.project_path` or doc-job snapshot, runs `os.path.realpath` + `os.path.isdir(.git)` checks, then runs git commands. There is NO allow-list check. The comment at lines 213-217 explicitly defers to "whatever wrote the Project record".

`terminal_service.validate_project_path` (lines 38-83) DOES block `/etc`, `/root`, `~/.ssh` etc. — but only at execution start. Doc generator does NOT call it.

**Risk**: If a Project record has malicious `path=/Users/eli/.ssh` (or any sensitive git repo), doc generator will:
- run `git diff HEAD` there
- include up to 6 KB raw diff body in AI prompt
- ship to external LLM (Anthropic/Ollama)
- persist portion to ExecutionSummary.summary, displayed to anyone viewing issue

**Fix**: Import `validate_project_path` from `terminal_service` and call at top of `_capture_git_changes`. Reject sensitive directories at doc-gen time, not just at exec start.

**Severity**: HIGH multi-tenant, MEDIUM single-operator.

Source: code-reviewer (H4) + security-auditor (H-2).

items.title: F3 [HIGH]: ImplementationNote.tags/references accept any JSON-array of strings, no per-item cap or URL validation
items.description:
**File**: `backend/models/schemas.py:600-613`

**Issue**: Pydantic validator only enforces top-level shape (≤10 KB JSON array of strings). No per-item length cap. The `references` column comment says "JSON array of file paths or URLs" but no URL validation — a `javascript:` URL stored here and later rendered without `defaultUrlTransform` would XSS.

Currently dormant: `ImplementationTab.tsx` does NOT render `tags` or `references`. Next consumer that renders these without `urlTransform` will be vulnerable.

**Fix**:
1. Add per-item length cap (e.g., 1000 chars per tag, 2000 per reference)
2. Add URL-shape validator to `references` (allow http://, https://, relative paths, reject javascript:/vbscript:/data:)
3. Document the contract on the column

Source: code-reviewer (H2).

items.title: F2 [HIGH]: No authz / rate-limit on /api/issues/{id}/documentation/* + /api/features/{id}/documentation/*
items.description:
**File**: `backend/api/documentation.py` (entire router)

**Issue**: `_ensure_issue_exists` and `_load_feature_issue` query only by `Issue.id` with no `projectId` constraint and no caller scoping. There is NO auth layer in the backend (`validate_origin` is CSRF defense, not authz). Any caller reachable on port 8401 can:
- POST /issues/{id}/documentation/notes → write 100 KB content per request, fill SQLite rapidly
- POST /features/{id}/documentation/generate → trigger AI call (most expensive endpoint), walk descendant tree (capped 5000)
- DELETE /issues/{id}/documentation/notes/{note_id} → silent deletion if note_id known/guessed

**Severity**: HIGH for multi-tenant, MEDIUM in current single-operator deployment. Existing comment in `models/schemas.py:589-591` already acknowledges "endpoint is unauthenticated".

**Fix options**:
1. Accept residual risk (single-operator) → document in comment, no code change
2. Add `projectId` scope to all `_ensure_*` lookups (cheap, doesn't add auth but reduces blast radius)
3. Full auth layer (out of scope of this feature, file separately)

**Recommendation**: Option 2 minimum — adds project-scoping which prevents cross-project IDOR even without user auth.

Source: code-reviewer (H1) + security-auditor (H-1).
items.implementationSummary:
Implemented CB-2117 (Option 2: projectId scoping) to address missing authorization scoping on the documentation API router. The core fix adds a required `?projectId=` query parameter to all 6 documentation endpoints (`/api/issues/{id}/documentation/*` and `/api/features/{id}/documentation/*`), and the internal helpers `_ensure_issue_exists` and `_load_feature_issue` now scope their SQLite lookups on both `Issue.id` AND `Issue.projectId`, preventing cross-project IDOR.

On the frontend, 5 React Query hooks in `useCodeBoard.ts` were updated to require `projectId` (queries are disabled until both the issue id and projectId are present), and a new `_docPath` helper centralises `?projectId=encodeURIComponent(...)` construction to defend against HTTP parameter pollution. Six component files were updated to thread `issue.projectId` through props and hook call sites, with loading shells rendering gracefully before the issue resolves and action buttons staying disabled until projectId is available.

The test suite in `test_documentation_api.py` was comprehensively updated: every existing URL was threaded with the new required `projectId` param, and 9 new IDOR-prevention tests were added including a parametrised suite covering all 7 method+path pairs for missing-projectId 422 responses, wrong-projectId 404 responses for every endpoint, DB row-count assertions confirming cross-project POST/DELETE are rejected, and an AI-spy assertion confirming `generate_text` is NOT invoked on cross-project generate requests. All 64 documentation API tests pass; 133 wider documentation suite tests pass; 781 backend tests pass overall with 2 pre-existing unrelated failures. Frontend `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

items.title: F1 [CRITICAL]: Completion loop atomicity — batch failure loses ExecutionSummaries + status updates
items.description:
**File**: `backend/app/main.py:122-134` (process_pending_completions)

**Issue**: `process_pending_completions` iterates all `pending_session_ids` inside ONE `AsyncSessionLocal()` and calls `db.commit()` only once at the end. If any iteration raises uncaught exception (flush IntegrityError, transient driver error), the outer `except Exception` skips commit — but `terminal_service.check_pending_completion()` already POPPED the pending flag (terminal_service.py:888) and `consume_pending_doc_job()` POPPED the doc-job (terminal_service.py:903). Net: those sessions' status updates and ExecutionSummary rows are lost AND will never be retried. Doc-jobs are unrecoverable (in-memory only).

**Reproduction**:
1. 3 AI executions complete in same 2-second loop tick
2. Session 2's flush raises IntegrityError (e.g., race on Issue.implementationSummary)
3. Outer except catches, skips commit
4. Sessions 1, 2, 3 ALL lose status update + summary + doc-job — never retried

**Fix**: Either (a) wrap each `_process_completion_for_session` in its own transaction (begin/commit/rollback per session) or (b) re-enqueue pending flags + doc-jobs on outer-except instead of just logging. Preferred: (a).

**Severity**: CRITICAL — silent data loss.

Source: code-reviewer audit CB-2102.

items.description: Manual: delete note → list refreshes without it → reload → confirmed gone.
items.implementationSummary:
CB-2113 is a QA regression task verifying that deleting an ImplementationNote returns HTTP 204 and the list refreshes without the deleted note, persisting after reload. The execution performed a full 7-point backend regression test by writing and running a Python script (`2026-05-07-cb2113-delete-note-regression.py`) that exercised POST→GET→DELETE→GET-refresh→GET-reload→DELETE-again→cross-issue-DELETE flows. items.description: Manual: note timestamp → regenerate → timestamp newer.
items.implementationSummary:
This was a pure QA verification task (CB-2077) with no intentional code changes. The goal was to manually verify that the `lastIndexedAt` timestamp on a FeatureDocumentation record updates after triggering a regeneration. The AI executed the verification end-to-end: captured the initial timestamp on FEATURE CB-2038 (`2026-05-06T22:14:06.024676`), triggered POST `/generate`, and confirmed the new timestamp (`2026-05-06T22:46:59.675402`) was newer — a ~33-minute advancement confirming the data-level acceptance criterion passed.

During visual QA in the browser, a timezone bug was discovered: the backend emits naive UTC ISO timestamps without a `Z` suffix, causing JavaScript's `new Date()` to interpret them as local time (Asia/Jerusalem, UTC+3), resulting in relative timestamps displaying '3h ago' instead of 'just now'. This was filed as a separate bug ticket CB-2377 with both backend and frontend fix candidates identified.

QA artifacts were persisted to durable paths: a markdown report at `docs/research/cb-2077-qa-report.md`, a screenshot at `docs/research/cb-2077-doc-page-after-regenerate.png`, and a push script at `scripts/codeboard/2026-05-07-CB-2077-qa-cwq-and-bug.py`. Audit path-traversal risk in chroma migration script. Verify `/api/system/rag/status` doesn't leak collection contents (only counts).

---

## Security audit complete (2026-05-02)

**Verdict: SAFE TO SHIP** — 0 CRITICAL, 0 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM, 2 LOW, 3 INFO. MEDIUMs/LOWs are defence-in-depth follow-ups, not release blockers on a localhost-only single-user platform.

**Audit targets covered (per CB-2049 task description):**
1. Path-traversal risk in chroma migration → bounded; runbook flagged for future-reuse hardening (L-1).
2. `/api/system/rag/status` data exposure → response shape correctly minimal (no documents/embeddings/metadatas/queries leak); `host` field overloaded with absolute filesystem path in PERSISTENT mode (M-1); collection-name list enables project enumeration (M-2). Confirmed via `RagStatusResponse` + `get_status_payload()` review.
3. Endpoint authz → effectively unauthenticated for non-browser callers (Origin middleware permits no-Origin server-to-server). Acceptable for current threat model but flagged for tightening (M-1, M-2).

**Findings filed as child BUGs under STORY CB-2047:**
- CB-2216 [MEDIUM]
- CB-2217 [MEDIUM]
- CB-2218 [MEDIUM]
- CB-2219 [LOW]
- CB-2220 [LOW]

**INFO-level (no follow-up needed):**
- I-1: TOCTOU during half-init not exploitable — lifespan blocks startup until init returns; `app.state.rag` only assigned after one path completes.
- I-2: Status response shape correctly minimal — no documents, embeddings, metadatas, query results, or issue keys leak. Logger output goes to backend logs only.
- I-3: Frontend card uses no credentials, no error leak — `fetch()` same-origin without `credentials: 'include'`; `console.error` logs only `Error.message`.

**Reviewed scope:**
- `backend/services/rag_service.py` (init/fallback/status payload/path constant)
- `backend/api/system.py` (status endpoint + Pydantic models)
- `backend/api/deps.py` (`RAGDep` provider)
- `backend/api/__init__.py` (system_router registration)
- `backend/app/main.py` (lifespan RAG init; `validate_origin` middleware authz)
- `frontend/components/service-monitor.tsx` (`RagStatusCard` polling + render)
- `docs/runbooks/2026-05-02-chroma-volume-migration.md` (migration commands)

Five child BUG tickets were filed under STORY CB-2047: CB-2216 (MEDIUM — `host` field leaks absolute filesystem path in PERSISTENT mode), CB-2217 (MEDIUM — collection names enable project enumeration), CB-2218 (MEDIUM — DoS amplification via heartbeat + per-collection polling), CB-2219 (LOW — migration runbook `tar` not hardened with `--no-same-owner`/`--anchored`), and CB-2220 (LOW — `PERSISTENT_FALLBACK_PATH` is CWD-relative). items.implementationSummary:
Implemented a new `RagStatusCard` subcomponent inside `frontend/components/service-monitor.tsx` that displays RAG service status as a persistent floating card in the bottom-left corner of the UI. The card polls `/api/system/rag/status` every 30 seconds and shows a mode badge (green for HTTP+healthy, amber for PERSISTENT or HTTP+unhealthy, red for UNINITIALIZED or repeated fetch failures), total document count, and an expandable view with endpoint details and top-3 collections by count.

The implementation follows the existing service-monitor polling pattern using `setInterval` with a ref-callback approach. A `normalizeRagStatus` runtime guard was added to prevent malformed API payloads from crashing the always-on card. A fail-threshold of 2 consecutive poll failures is required before flipping to the red 'RAG offline' state to prevent flickering on transient network hiccups. The card is hidden below the `sm` breakpoint (`hidden sm:block`) to avoid mobile layout collisions.

All audit gates were passed: TypeScript type-check was clean for the modified file, ESLint reported no new issues, a code-reviewer pass addressed 2 HIGH and 2 MEDIUM findings (chevron direction, mobile collision, PERSISTENT label, error flicker), and a security-auditor pass found 0 CRITICAL/HIGH issues with the one MEDIUM runtime-type-confusion risk addressed via the normalize guard. Five UI states were visually verified via Chrome DevTools mock fetch injection: HTTP+healthy (green), HTTP+unhealthy (amber), PERSISTENT (amber with Path label), UNINITIALIZED (red), and fetch-fail-after-2-polls (red).

items.title: T1.2.1: Endpoint GET /api/system/rag/status
items.description: Returns `{mode: 'HTTP'|'PERSISTENT', host: str, port: int, collections: [{name, count}], total_docs: int, healthy: bool}`. Read-only. No auth required (already internal).
items.implementationSummary:
Implemented the `GET /api/system/rag/status` read-only endpoint (CB-2045) that returns a structured payload describing the RAG subsystem's current state: connection mode (HTTP or PERSISTENT), host, port, per-collection document counts, total document count, and a health boolean.

The work involved three layers: a new `get_status_payload()` method on `RAGService` that traps all Chroma calls and never raises (logging heartbeat and list-collections failures at WARNING level after a code-reviewer finding), a new FastAPI router at `backend/api/system.py` with a `RagStatusResponse` Pydantic model, and registration of that router in `backend/api/__init__.py`. Fourteen new unit and endpoint tests were added covering uninitialised state, HTTP mode, PERSISTENT mode, and failure paths, all passing alongside the full regression suite.

Two audit gates were run in parallel: a code-review agent (applied one MEDIUM fix — elevated silent failure log level to WARNING; deferred style/IPv6 LOWs) and a security-audit agent (zero CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM findings; two LOW info-disclosure items accepted as within the existing Origin-validation trust boundary). The ticket was transitioned to COMPLETED_WAITING_QA via the Rule 29 per-project script. The backend requires a restart to surface the new endpoint in the live process.

items.title: T1.1.3: Add startup log line surfacing RAG mode (HTTP vs PERSISTENT)
items.description: In `app/main.py` lifespan + `services/rag_service.py`: log `RAG mode=HTTP host=chromadb port=8000 collections=N` or `RAG mode=PERSISTENT path=... collections=N`. Currently fallback is silent, which is how we ended up with embedded sqlite chroma without realizing it.
items.implementationSummary:
Implemented startup log lines that surface the RAG mode (HTTP vs PERSISTENT) in `backend/services/rag_service.py` and `backend/app/main.py`. The `RAGService` class was extended with `_mode` and `_mode_detail` instance attributes, a module-level `PERSISTENT_FALLBACK_PATH` constant, and a new `describe_mode()` method that returns a human-readable string like `RAG mode=HTTP host=localhost port=8402 collections=8` or `RAG mode=PERSISTENT path=/abs/path/data/chroma collections=8`. Both `_init_client_blocking` and `_fallback_to_persistent` now reset and set these attributes so the correct mode is always reflected regardless of which path was taken.

The lifespan handler in `main.py` was updated to call `logger.info('[startup] %s', rag.describe_mode())` after the RAG service initializes or falls back, using parameterized logging to avoid any f-string injection risk. Collection count is retrieved via `client.list_collections()` inside `describe_mode()` and falls back to `?` on any error, ensuring the log call never blocks or raises during startup.

A new test file `tests/test_rag_service_describe_mode.py` was added with 4 cases covering: uninitialized state, HTTP success path, persistent fallback path, and swallowed count-failure path. The full RAG-adjacent regression suite (19 tests including stability regression) remained green. Two LOW findings from the code reviewer were remediated: the exception-swallowing branch had its `# pragma: no cover` removed, and defensive state resets were added at the top of both `_init_client_blocking` and `_fallback_to_persistent` to prevent stale `_mode` being paired with a `None` client after a mid-init exception.

items.title: T1.1.2: Migrate backend/data/chroma/* to container volume chroma_data
items.description: Copy existing collections (7 UUID dirs + chroma.sqlite3, 17MB) from local fallback path into the container's `/chroma/chroma` mount. Verify collection counts match before/after. If migration is unsafe, document why and accept fresh start.
items.implementationSummary:
CB-2042 migrated 17 MB of ChromaDB embeddings from the local fallback path `backend/data/chroma/` into the `projectsmanagerwebv2production_chroma_data` Docker volume served by the chromadb container at `127.0.0.1:8402`. The migration was performed as a copy (not a move), preserving the original data for rollback safety.

The process involved stopping the chromadb container for a clean SQLite close, verifying the destination volume was empty, and transferring data via `tar -cf - | docker run -i ... tar xf -` stdin pipe (direct bind-mount failed due to Colima file-sharing restrictions on `/Volumes/Seagate`). After restarting chromadb and confirming heartbeat, all 8 collections were verified present with counts matching baseline exactly: `1833 / 796 / 718 / 0×5`. Per-file byte parity was confirmed for every UUID directory and `chroma.sqlite3` (18,182,144 bytes); an earlier `du -sh` size discrepancy was traced to APFS-vs-ext4 block-size reporting differences, not data loss.

A functional regression check queried real embeddings from the largest collection (`project_1511e54f`) and returned a valid document with metadata. The backend's `chromadb.HttpClient(host, port)` uses default tenant/database, confirmed compatible with the volume namespace. Two artifacts were produced per Bible Rules 27 and 29: a migration runbook at `docs/runbooks/2026-05-02-chroma-volume-migration.md` and a per-project status update script at `scripts/codeboard/2026-05-02-CB-2042-mark-cwq.py`. CB-2042 was marked COMPLETED_WAITING_QA.

items.title: T1.1.1: Run docker compose up chromadb, verify port 8402 reachable + heartbeat
items.description: Start chromadb service via docker-compose. Verify `curl http://localhost:8402/api/v2/heartbeat` returns 200. Confirm backend rag_service connects via HTTP mode (not PERSISTENT fallback).
items.implementationSummary: Restored chromadb container availability. Colima docker socket had gone stale; `colima restart` brought the daemon back, and the chromadb container auto-started via its `restart: unless-stopped` policy (image chromadb/chroma:0.6.3, container name projectsmanagerwebv2production-chromadb-1). Verified the service end-to-end: `curl http://localhost:8402/api/v2/heartbeat` returns HTTP 200 with body `{"nanosecond heartbeat":1777751663389999091}`. Backend env (backend/.env, backend/app/config.py) already targets localhost:8402, and the lifespan path in backend/app/main.py (lines 256-269) calls rag._init_client_blocking() first - which does a 5s TCP probe and a heartbeat() call - and only falls back to PersistentClient on exception. items.implementationSummary:
Implemented progressive disclosure (Miller's Law) for the `LinkedIssuesPanel` component. A new constant `VISIBLE_PER_GROUP = 5` caps the default visible rows per relation-type section, with a component-local `useState<Set<LinkType>>` tracking which sections are expanded — each section toggles independently. When a group has more than 5 rows, a `+ N more` button appears; clicking it expands that group inline and switches to a `Show less` label. The section heading always shows the full total count for transparency.

Accessibility was addressed with native `<button>` elements (free keyboard activation via Enter/Space), `aria-expanded` state, and `aria-controls` attributes pointing to the list container. IDs are prefixed with `issueId` to prevent collisions when two panels co-exist on the same page. A security audit confirmed no new attack surface — `linkType` is a closed enum so no user-controlled string interpolation occurs in DOM ids.

Six new unit-test cases were added covering: the boundary condition at exactly 5 rows (no button), the `+ N more` label and count, expand/collapse toggle cycle, per-group independence, `aria-controls` DOM resolution, and keyboard (Enter) activation. After applying audit feedback (id-collision fix, aria-controls, keyboard test), the full suite passed at **17/17**. TypeScript reported no new errors in changed files. CB-2000 was marked `COMPLETED_WAITING_QA`.

Implemented `DELETE /api/groups/{group_id}/members` — a body-based bulk remove endpoint that accepts `{issueIds: [str]}` and returns `{removed: int, notFound: [str]}`. The implementation mirrors the sibling CB-1989 bulk-add pattern: a Pydantic request schema with deduplication, min/max validation, 64-char id cap, and `extra=forbid`, plus a response schema with `removed` count and `notFound` list.

The endpoint logic: validates the group exists (404 otherwise), SELECTs existing `IssueGroupMember` rows for the requested ids scoped to the group, partitions into `existing` vs `notFound` (lumping both 'issue doesn't exist' and 'issue not in group' into `notFound`), executes a fused DELETE scoped by `(groupId, issueId IN existing)`, and returns `removed = rowcount`. Issues themselves are untouched — only the `GroupMember` join row is deleted.

A 12-test suite (`test_groups_members_delete.py`) covers: happy path, partial removal, all-not-found, deduplication, 404 group, cross-group isolation, issue-survives assertion, and 422 validation cases. All 12 new tests and 56 existing groups tests pass. Two audit agents (code-reviewer + security-auditor) returned clean with only LOW doc-level nits, which were addressed by tightening inline comments.

items.title: DELETE /api/groups/{group_id}
items.description: Cascades IssueGroupMember rows. Issues survive. Reject (409) if any member still IN_PROGRESS — Reader rule from Web Security book p. 15.
items.implementationSummary:
Implemented `DELETE /api/groups/{group_id}` endpoint (CB-1987) with full cascade semantics and a 409 guard for in-progress work. The endpoint deletes the group and cascades removal of all `IssueGroupMember` rows via `ondelete=CASCADE`, while leaving the underlying `Issue` records untouched. A 404 is returned for missing groups and a 409 with `inProgressIssueIds` + `inProgressIssueKeys` payload is returned if any member issue is `IN_PROGRESS`.

A TOCTOU race condition flagged by parallel code-reviewer and security-auditor agents was resolved by collapsing the guard SELECT and the DELETE into a single atomic statement: `DELETE … WHERE id = :id AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM IssueGroupMember m JOIN Issue i … WHERE i.status = 'IN_PROGRESS')`. On `rowcount == 0` the handler re-scans within the same transaction to disambiguate a 404 (group never existed or already deleted) from a 409 (guard correctly suppressed the delete). The live-work status string was centralised as `_LIVE_WORK_STATUS` module constant.

Six targeted tests were written in `test_groups_delete.py` covering: 204 on empty group, 204 cascade with issue survival, 404 missing group, 409 guard with offender details, cross-group isolation, and per-group guard scoping. All 53 tests across the groups test suite pass green. CB-1987 was marked `COMPLETED_WAITING_QA` via the API.

items.title: GET /api/groups/{group_id} (detail)

items.implementationSummary:
Implemented the `GET /api/groups/{group_id}` detail endpoint for CB-1986. The endpoint returns an `IssueGroupDetailResponse` containing aggregate status information (`statusBreakdown`, `completionPercent`, `dominantStatus`) and a `members` array of `IssueGroupMemberResponse` objects (each with `id`, `issueId`, `issue` summary, `position`, `addedAt`) ordered by `(position ASC, id ASC)` for deterministic tie-breaking.

The implementation uses a two-level `selectinload` (`members` → `issue`) to avoid N+1 queries given the `lazy="raise_on_sql"` constraint on the relationship. Aggregate status is delegated entirely to the existing `compute_group_status` helper (introduced in CB-1958) to keep tie-break and CANCELLED-denominator semantics single-sourced. A 404 `NotFoundError("IssueGroup", group_id)` is raised for missing groups, matching the structured error pattern of sibling endpoints.

Seven tests were written covering: happy path with ordered members and embedded `IssueSummary`, empty group, out-of-order positions, same-position tie-breaking by member id, all-complete aggregate (100%), issue summary field leak guard, and 404 for missing group. All 7 pass. Dual audit gates (code-reviewer + security-auditor) were run in parallel; 0 CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM findings. Two should-fix items were addressed: same-position determinism test added and an orphan-guard comment added to the endpoint. Regression suite showed 588/591 passing with 3 pre-existing unrelated failures confirmed via git stash.

items.implementationSummary:
Implemented `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/groups` endpoint (CB-1984) to allow creating issue groups within a project. The endpoint accepts a JSON body with `title`, optional `description`, and optional `issueIds` array, validates that the project exists (404), that all referenced issues exist (404), and that all member issues belong to the same project (400 with `details.invalidIssueIds`). On success it returns `201` with the full `IssueGroupResponse` including `memberCount`.

A new router module `backend/api/groups.py` (~175 lines) was created following the same patterns as the existing `relations.py` sibling. The schema `IssueGroupCreate` caps `issueIds` at 500 entries, individual ids at 64 chars, and description at 10k chars — Pydantic enforces these as 422s before business logic runs. Member positions are assigned 1..N in Python to avoid the `next_member_position` same-session pitfall identified in `models/grouping.py:135`. An `IntegrityError` is surfaced as a typed `DatabaseError` per the security-auditor M1 fix.

The router was wired into `backend/api/__init__.py`. Eight targeted tests were written in `backend/tests/test_groups_post.py` covering: happy path, missing project, missing issue, cross-project issue, empty issueIds, schema violations (too-long title, oversized list), and duplicate ids. All 8 pass; 199/199 tests pass across the grouping, relations, and schema-integrity suites. Two pre-existing unrelated failures in `test_qa_sequence.py` and `test_schema_validation.py` (AgentProfile / aiContext drift) were confirmed not introduced by this change. Code-reviewer and security-auditor both returned PASS.

items.description: Two issues from different projects → 400. Same project → 201.
items.implementationSummary:
CB-1981 was a test-only task to lock the same-project enforcement contract for issue relations. A dedicated test file `backend/tests/test_relations_cross_project.py` was created with 23 tests covering all cross-project rejection scenarios across both single POST and bulk POST endpoints.

The tests cover: per-LinkType sweep (all 7 values) verifying cross-project requests return 400 and same-project returns 201, transaction rollback verification (no rows persisted on rejection), error envelope shape pinning, cross-project validation ordering relative to duplicate checks, bulk atomicity (no partial inserts on mixed batches), and a security regression guard ensuring legacy cross-project rows never leak via the bulk duplicate-skip channel.

All 23 tests passed in the new file, and the full relations regression suite of 119 tests passed with no collateral damage. Two audit gates (code-reviewer and security-auditor) approved the work. Auditor-flagged HIGH and LOW items were addressed within the file. Two follow-up tickets (CB-2126, CB-2127) were filed for MEDIUM gaps in unrelated endpoints (GET/DELETE), and CB-1981 was marked COMPLETED_WAITING_QA.

items.title: Service-layer same-project check + clean 400 error
items.description: Reuse projectId comparison. Apply to both single + bulk endpoints.
items.implementationSummary:
CB-1980 required adding a service-layer same-project check to both the single and bulk relation-creation endpoints, returning a clean HTTP 400 error when a caller attempts to link issues from different projects.

The implementation was found to already exist in `backend/api/relations.py` as part of prior work on CB-1971/CB-1972. The single endpoint (lines 281-289) fetches both issues' projectIds in one round-trip and raises a `ValidationError` → HTTP 400 with message `"Cannot link issues from different projects"` and details containing `fromProjectId` and `toProjectId`. The bulk endpoint (lines 565-585) partitions invalid pairs (self-link, missing target, cross-project) into a unified `invalid_ids` set and raises a matching 400 with `details.invalidIds`.

Verification consisted of running the full relations test suite (96/96 passing), confirming coverage via `test_cross_project_rejected` and `test_bulk_400_when_cross_project`, and applying audit gates. A MEDIUM security finding (cross-tenant oracle: 404 vs 400 on single endpoint leaks issue existence across tenants) was flagged to Eli as a CB-1971 contract concern out of scope for this ticket. The ticket was marked COMPLETED_WAITING_QA.

items.implementationSummary: Added backend/tests/test_relations_cycle.py — 22 tests covering: _has_cycle helper unit tests (empty graph, disjoint, length-2/3 cycles, family scoping, cross-project skip), _canonical_edge direction (BLOCKS/CAUSES preserve, IS_BLOCKED_BY/CAUSED_BY flip), parametrized A→A self-link rejection across all 7 LinkTypes, CAUSED_BY 3-cycle (filling gap left by test_relations_post.py), same-DB-state transitive-vs-symmetric comparison (A BLOCKS B then B→A: BLOCKS rejects with 409 CYCLE_DETECTED, RELATES_TO/DUPLICATES/IS_DUPLICATED_BY all 201), DUPLICATES 3-chain non-cycle, _TRANSITIVE_FAMILIES membership lock-down. All 22 pass; full relations suite 96/96 pass. Code-review (medium tightened to LIFO-pinned comment, two missing pair-set assertions added) and security-audit gates: clean.

items.title: Wire cycle check into POST /relations + bulk
items.description: Run check before INSERT. Same DB transaction. 409 with `code: CYCLE_DETECTED` and `details.path` on detection.
items.implementationSummary:
Implemented the cycle detection contract for `POST /relations` and the bulk relations endpoint as specified in CB-1977. The core change was upgrading `_has_cycle` from returning a boolean to returning `Optional[list[str]]` — the closed cycle path — so callers can surface `details.path` in the 409 response. A new `CycleDetectedError` (HTTP 409) and `CYCLE_DETECTED` error code were added to the errors module.

The single `POST /relations` endpoint now raises `CycleDetectedError` with a structured `details` envelope containing `fromIssueId`, `toIssueId`, `linkType`, `path`, and optionally `truncated: true` when the path exceeds 50 nodes. The bulk endpoint uses the same helper with `is not None` semantics and silently skips cycles with `reason: CYCLE` as before, but now benefits from the same security fixes.

Two audit findings were addressed in the same diff: a MEDIUM cross-project data leak (BFS now JOINs `Issue` and filters by `project_id` so cycle traversal cannot surface IDs from other projects) and a LOW unbounded-path DoS risk (50-node cap with `_truncate_cycle_path` and an ellipsis sentinel). 74/74 relations tests pass; 3 pre-existing unrelated failures (qa_sequence + AgentProfile/aiContext schema drift) were confirmed untouched.

items.title: STORY 2.2 — Cycle-detection helper
items.description:
Recursive CTE reachability check, runs inside the write transaction. Applies only to asymmetric transitive types (BLOCKS, IS_BLOCKED_BY, CAUSED_BY, CAUSES). RELATES_TO and DUPLICATES are symmetric — no cycle check.

**Algorithm** (per Reader's Code Review v4 + Web Security findings):
WITH RECURSIVE reachable(id) AS (
  SELECT toIssueId FROM IssueLink WHERE fromIssueId=:newTarget AND linkType IN ('BLOCKS','CAUSED_BY')
  UNION ALL
  SELECT il.toIssueId FROM IssueLink il JOIN reachable r ON il.fromIssueId=r.id WHERE il.linkType IN ('BLOCKS','CAUSED_BY')
)
SELECT 1 FROM reachable WHERE id=:newSource LIMIT 1;
-- If row → cycle → reject 409

items.title: DELETE /api/issues/{id}/relations/{relation_id}
items.description: Either participant can delete. Auto-deletes companion inverse row in same txn. Response `{deleted: 2}`.
items.implementationSummary:
Implemented `DELETE /api/issues/{id}/relations/{relation_id}` endpoint as specified in CB-1974. The endpoint allows either participant of a relation to delete it, automatically deleting the companion inverse row in the same transaction, and returns `{deleted: <int>}` where 2 indicates both primary and companion rows were removed and 1 indicates a legacy orphan row.

The implementation extended `backend/api/relations.py` with a `delete_relation` handler that performs a SELECT-by-id, validates participant scope, then executes an atomic delete covering both the primary and inverse rows. Race conditions (concurrent deletes) surface as 404 via rowcount=0 + rollback. Unknown linkTypes return 500 DATABASE_ERROR with relational context in the details body as a corrupt-data signal. A new `IssueLinkDeleteResponse` Pydantic schema with `deleted: int = Field(ge=1, le=2)` enforces bounds at the schema layer.

Two parallel audit agents (code-reviewer + security-auditor) were run after initial implementation. All MEDIUM findings were addressed: DatabaseError mapped to 500, schema bounds tightened, cross-project comment added, and security regression tests written. Final test count was 20 in `test_relations_delete.py` (up from 0), with 71/71 passing across all 4 relations test files covering happy paths, both-participant URLs, companion-id symmetry, all 7 LinkType values parametrized, orphan companion, 404 variants, idempotency, and no participant-id leakage.

items.title: GET /api/issues/{id}/relations
items.description: Returns `{outbound: [...], inbound: [...]}`. Each item has fromIssue/toIssue summaries. Default cap pageSize=100.
items.implementationSummary:
Implemented `GET /api/issues/{issue_id}/relations` endpoint (CB-1973) that returns a structured response `{outbound: [...], inbound: [...]}` where each item carries full `fromIssue`/`toIssue` summaries. Outbound rows are those where `fromIssueId == issue_id`; inbound where `toIssueId == issue_id`. Both lists are ordered deterministically by `createdAt DESC, id DESC` and capped per-direction at `pageSize` (default 100, range 1–100, Pydantic-validated 422 on violation). A 404 is returned when the source issue does not exist. Eager-loading via `selectinload` respects the ORM's `lazy="raise_on_sql"` contract.

A new `IssueRelationsListResponse` schema was added to `backend/models/schemas.py` and exported through `backend/models/__init__.py`. The router in `backend/api/relations.py` received the new `list_relations` handler, and `backend/api/__init__.py` was updated to expose the route. A dedicated test file `backend/tests/test_relations_get.py` was created with 13 tests covering: happy path, empty lists, 404 on missing issue, pageSize default/cap/range validation, deterministic ordering, per-direction split, cross-project isolation, and embedded summary fields.

Two audit gates were run in parallel (code-reviewer + security-auditor) after initial implementation. The code-reviewer flagged a dead constant `_ISSUE_LINK_LIST_MAX_PAGE` in schemas.py (fixed immediately). The security-auditor noted cross-tenant scoping as a pre-existing API posture shared by sibling POST endpoints (CB-1971/CB-1972), deferred to a whole-feature follow-up ticket. Full regression suite (102 tests across all relations test files + schema integrity tests) passed before marking CB-1973 COMPLETED_WAITING_QA.

items.title: POST /api/issues/{id}/relations/bulk
items.description: Body `{toIssueIds: [str], linkType}`. Returns `{created, skipped}`. Skips duplicates silently. 400 with `details.invalidIds` for bad ids.
items.implementationSummary:
Implemented `POST /api/issues/{id}/relations/bulk` endpoint (CB-1972) that accepts `{toIssueIds: [str], linkType}` and returns `{created, skipped}`. The endpoint supports creating up to 100 relations in a single atomic request, silently skipping duplicates with a `DUPLICATE` reason and transitive cycles with a `CYCLE` reason, while returning 400 with `details.invalidIds` for self-links, missing issues, or cross-project targets.

Three new Pydantic schemas were added — `IssueLinkBulkCreate`, `IssueLinkBulkSkipped`, and `IssueLinkBulkResponse` — alongside a constant `_ISSUE_LINK_BULK_MAX_TARGETS=100` and a regex validator per-id. The `_has_cycle` helper in `relations.py` was extended to accept a shared `budget` argument so that the entire batch shares one `_MAX_CYCLE_VISIT` ceiling (same as single-POST), closing a HIGH-severity DoS vector where 100 candidates × 5000 BFS visits could produce 500K SELECTs per request.

A dedicated test file `test_relations_post_bulk.py` was created with 19 tests covering happy path, deduplication, cycle detection, invalid IDs, shape validation, and the shared-budget DoS guard. All 38 relations tests and 72 sibling/grouping tests pass green. The security auditor flagged zero CRITICAL issues after the budget-sharing fix was applied.

items.title: Tests for aggregate over various member status mixes
items.description: Cover: all CWQ → completionPercent=100, dominantStatus=CWQ; mixed → percent < 100; empty group → all zeros; group with single member.
items.implementationSummary:
CB-1968 required tests for `compute_group_status`, the helper implemented in CB-1967 that aggregates member statuses into a `GroupAggregateStatus` snapshot. A new test file `backend/tests/test_compute_group_status.py` was created with 13 pytest cases covering all four acceptance bullets from the issue: all-CWQ → completionPercent=100 and dominantStatus=CWQ; mixed statuses → percent < 100; empty group → all zeros; single-member groups (complete and incomplete).

Beyond the acceptance bullets, the suite also exercises helper-doc invariants: all-DONE group, CANCELLED counted in denominator, top-count-beats-lex tie-break, a dedicated 2-way lexicographic tie-break case, 2-decimal rounding precision, unknown group ID, cross-group isolation, and an orphaned-member INNER JOIN branch triggered via a raw parameterized insert that bypasses the ORM FK constraint. The fixture was refactored to expose the SQLAlchemy engine directly so the orphan insert could safely tear down after the test.

Audit gates were applied: the code-reviewer agent found 0 CRITICAL/HIGH issues and 3 MEDIUMs, of which 2 were resolved by splitting the tie-break test and adding the orphan-branch test; the security-auditor found no injection risk, no secrets, and safe tempfile teardown. All 13 new tests pass, and the full 33-test neighbourhood (including `test_apply_grouping_tables.py` and `test_cascade_status.py`) shows no regression. CB-1968 was PATCHed to COMPLETED_WAITING_QA on CodeBoard.

items.title: Implement compute_group_status in backend/utils/db_queries.py
items.description: Single SQL: SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM Issue JOIN IssueGroupMember ... WHERE groupId = :gid GROUP BY status. Return Pydantic-shaped dict.
items.implementationSummary:
Implemented `compute_group_status` async helper in `backend/utils/db_queries.py` (line ~971). The function executes a single parameterized SQL query joining `Issue` and `IssueGroupMember` on `issueId`, filtering by `groupId`, and grouping by `Issue.status` to produce status counts. Results are mapped into the existing `GroupAggregateStatus` Pydantic schema.

`completionPercent` is calculated as `(DONE + COMPLETED_WAITING_QA) / total * 100` rounded to 2 decimal places, matching the predicate used by `cascade_status_to_parents`. `dominantStatus` is determined by max-count with a deterministic lexicographic tie-break via `min()`. Empty or orphan-only groups return schema defaults (`{}`, `0.0`, `None`).

Two security/robustness hardening items were applied after the audit pass: a NULL-status guard filters out corrupted rows that would crash the `min()` comparison, and an inline docstring documents the IDOR contract requiring callers to scope on `IssueGroup.projectId` before invoking. All 59 pytest tests pass after both the initial implementation and the hardening patch.

items.title: STORY 1.3 — Aggregate-status helper for groups

Backend deltas:

items.title: Idempotent CREATE TABLE migration script
items.description: PMv2 has no Alembic. Add tables to `Base.metadata` imports and ensure `init_db()` creates them. For existing DBs, idempotent SQL via `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`.
items.implementationSummary:
CB-1964 implemented idempotent CREATE TABLE migration support for the `IssueGroup` and `IssueGroupMember` tables in PMv2, which has no Alembic. The core deliverable is `backend/utils/apply_grouping_tables.py`, an out-of-band migration script that uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` DDL so it can be run safely against both fresh and existing databases without errors or data loss.

The migration script mirrors the shape of the existing `apply_indexes.py` utility and creates all three indexes (`idx_issue_group_project`, `idx_issue_group_member_group`, `idx_issue_group_member_issue`) alongside the two tables. Credentials are redacted from the printed DB URL. The script was verified by running it twice against `frontend/prisma/dev.db`: first pass produced 5 created, second pass 5 skipped with 0 errors.

A full regression test suite (`backend/tests/test_apply_grouping_tables.py`, 5 tests, all green) was added covering: first-pass creation, idempotent second-pass skip, UNIQUE constraint enforcement, FK `ON DELETE` action correctness, and schema parity between the script and `Base.metadata.create_all`. `schema_test_utils.py` was also updated to include the grouping models and table entries so the broader schema integrity suite stays accurate.

items.title: Pydantic schemas: IssueGroupCreate, IssueGroupResponse, IssueGroupDetailResponse, IssueGroupMemberResponse, PaginatedGroupResponse
items.description: Per the api-designer contract. Detail response includes `aggregateStatus.{statusBreakdown, completionPercent, dominantStatus}` and `members` array with embedded issue summary.
items.implementationSummary:
CB-1963 implemented five Pydantic schemas (plus two supporting schemas) for the IssueGroup feature, per the api-designer contract. The schemas — `IssueGroupCreate`, `IssueGroupUpdate`, `IssueGroupResponse`, `IssueGroupMemberResponse`, `GroupAggregateStatus`, `IssueGroupDetailResponse`, and `PaginatedGroupResponse` — were added to `backend/models/schemas.py` and exported from `backend/models/__init__.py`. The `GroupAggregateStatus` model captures `statusBreakdown`, `completionPercent` (0–100), and `dominantStatus` as required by the spec; `IssueGroupDetailResponse` embeds it alongside a `members` array of `IssueGroupMemberResponse` objects that each carry an embedded issue summary.

Security hardening was applied following audit-gate findings: description fields are capped at 10,000 characters (MEDIUM), and `issueIds` entries are individually capped at 64 characters with a 500-item list cap, deduplication, and stripping via a `field_validator` (LOW/MEDIUM). The `memberCount` field is documented and tested as being set via `setattr` by the service layer before `model_validate` is called, matching the lazy-raise ORM pattern used for sibling schemas.

A `TestIssueGroupSchemas` class with 12 tests was appended to `backend/tests/test_schema_data_integrity.py`, covering round-trips, validator rejection paths, the memberCount setattr path, and the completionPercent boundary conditions. All 46 schema-integrity tests pass; pre-existing failures in `test_schema_validation` (unrelated `aiContext` column and unexpected-tables issues) were confirmed present on main before any changes.

items.title: SQLAlchemy models for IssueGroup + IssueGroupMember
items.description: New file `backend/models/grouping.py`. FK to Project (RESTRICT on delete), FK to Issue (CASCADE on delete). Indexes on groupId + issueId. UniqueConstraint(groupId, issueId).
items.implementationSummary:
Implemented two new SQLAlchemy ORM models — `IssueGroup` and `IssueGroupMember` — in a new file `backend/models/grouping.py`, fulfilling CB-1962. `IssueGroup` holds a title, description, and a foreign key to `Project` with `ON DELETE RESTRICT` semantics. `IssueGroupMember` joins a group to an issue with `ON DELETE CASCADE` on both FKs, a named `UniqueConstraint(groupId, issueId)`, and individual indexes on both `groupId` and `issueId` columns.

Both models were registered in `backend/models/__init__.py` (package import + `__all__`). The `IssueGroupMember.issue` back-reference was configured as `lazy="raise_on_sql"` (matching the CB-1960 IssueLink pattern) to prevent async N+1 surprises and force explicit `selectinload` at call sites. A post-review belt-and-braces fix applied `passive_deletes=True` to the cascade back-ref.

DDL was validated against an in-memory SQLite engine confirming FK `ondelete` clauses, indexes, and the named unique constraint. All 34 existing schema integrity tests passed with no regressions. CB-1962 was marked `COMPLETED_WAITING_QA`; the `position` field was intentionally deferred to sibling task CB-1965 per the CodeBoard story split.

items.title: STORY 1.2 — New IssueGroup + IssueGroupMember tables
items.description:
New entities mirror the QATaskIssueLink shape (id, fk, fk, createdAt + indexes).

**IssueGroup** (id, projectId, title, description, createdAt, updatedAt) — no stored status field; computed on read in v1.
**IssueGroupMember** (id, groupId, issueId, position, createdAt) with `UniqueConstraint(groupId, issueId)`.

Position field included now to support drag-to-reorder later — retrofitting ordering on a paginated table is painful.

items.title: Extend IssueLinkResponse with fromIssue + toIssue summary projections
items.description: Embed `{id, key, title, status}` summaries for both ends so frontend renders relation cards without a second round-trip. Read-only projections, never written.
items.implementationSummary:
CB-1960 extended `IssueLinkResponse` with read-only `fromIssue` and `toIssue` summary projections so the frontend can render relation cards without a second round-trip. A new `IssueSummary` Pydantic model (`id`, `key`, `title`, `status`) was introduced in `models/schemas.py`, and `IssueLinkResponse` gained two optional fields (`fromIssue: Optional[IssueSummary]`, `toIssue: Optional[IssueSummary]`) defaulting to `None` for full backward compatibility.

On the ORM side, `models/issue.py` received two SQLAlchemy relationships (`fromIssue`, `toIssue`) on the `IssueLink` model configured with `lazy="raise_on_sql"` to prevent silent N+1 queries — callers must explicitly use `selectinload` to hydrate the projections. `models/__init__.py` was updated to export `IssueSummary`. A parallel code-review + security-audit pass caught two MEDIUM findings: the `lazy` strategy choice (applied) and a `status: str` typing tightening (applied); no CRITICAL/HIGH issues were found.

Two new tests were added to `tests/test_schema_data_integrity.py` — a positive selectinload projection test and a transient-instance None-default test — bringing the IssueLink suite to 6/6 green and the broader schema regression suite to 53/53 pass. Two pre-existing failures (`AgentProfile` table and `aiContext` column tests) were confirmed unrelated to this diff. The ticket was moved to `COMPLETED_WAITING_QA`.

items.title: Add UniqueConstraint(fromIssueId, toIssueId, linkType) to IssueLink
items.description: Prevents duplicate identical relations. SQLAlchemy `UniqueConstraint` in `__table_args__`. Migration via `apply_indexes.py` or `Base.metadata.create_all()`.
items.implementationSummary:
CB-1959 added a `UniqueConstraint` on `(fromIssueId, toIssueId, linkType)` to the `IssueLink` SQLAlchemy model, enforcing ORM-level duplicate-relation prevention that mirrors the existing Prisma-generated unique index already present in the database. The constraint name was deliberately matched to Prisma's generated index name (`IssueLink_fromIssueId_toIssueId_linkType_key`) to ensure parity between the ORM layer and the underlying SQLite schema.

A defensive entry was added to `apply_indexes.py` so that backends which are not managed by Prisma migrations will also receive the unique index idempotently via `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`. The script pre-checks `PRAGMA index_list` to skip creation when the index already exists, making the operation safe to re-run.

Two new tests were added to `test_schema_data_integrity.py`: `test_duplicate_issue_link_fails` (confirms an `IntegrityError` is raised on duplicate insert) and `test_different_link_type_allowed` (confirms that the same `(fromIssueId, toIssueId)` pair with a different `linkType` is accepted). All 79 schema tests pass and a live ad-hoc test against the frontend dev.db confirmed the constraint is enforced at runtime.

items.title: Extend LinkType enum: add CAUSED_BY + CAUSES
items.description: Add the two missing semantic types to the existing `LinkType` enum in `backend/models/schemas.py` and the SQLAlchemy column type. `CAUSED_BY` and `CAUSES` are inverse pair, like BLOCKS/IS_BLOCKED_BY.
items.implementationSummary:
Extended the `LinkType` enum in `backend/models/schemas.py` by adding two new semantic link types: `CAUSED_BY` and `CAUSES`. These form an inverse pair analogous to the existing `BLOCKS`/`IS_BLOCKED_BY` and `DUPLICATES`/`IS_DUPLICATED_BY` pairs, bringing the total enum values to 7.

The `IssueLink.linkType` column is stored as a plain `Column(String)` in SQLAlchemy — not a native SQL enum or check constraint — so no database migration was required. The Pydantic enum in `schemas.py` serves as the sole allowlist, and the change is purely additive.

Supporting comment updates were made in `backend/models/issue.py` and `frontend/prisma/schema.prisma` to enumerate all 7 link types. Verification included `py_compile` checks, runtime Pydantic coercion tests in the project venv, and 4 passing schema data integrity tests. Both the code-reviewer and security-auditor audit gates returned APPROVED with no critical or high findings.

items.title: STORY 1.1 — Wire existing IssueLink table (extend, don't fork)
items.description:
The IssueLink table at `backend/models/issue.py:158-174` already has shape `(id, fromIssueId, toIssueId, linkType, createdAt)` with FK indexes. The `IssueLinkCreate` and `IssueLinkResponse` Pydantic schemas already exist in `backend/models/schemas.py`. The `LinkType` enum already has BLOCKS, IS_BLOCKED_BY, RELATES_TO, DUPLICATES, IS_DUPLICATED_BY. Nothing wired to API.

Task: extend the enum, add the unique constraint, and finalise the response shape with embedded summaries.

items.title: EPIC 1 — Data model: relations + groups schema
items.description:
Wire the existing `IssueLink` table, add new `IssueGroup` + `IssueGroupMember` tables, and the aggregate-status helper.

**Files involved**:
- `backend/models/issue.py:158-174` (IssueLink — already defined, just extend LinkType enum + add unique constraint)
- `backend/models/grouping.py` (new — IssueGroup + IssueGroupMember models)
- `backend/models/schemas.py` (new Pydantic shapes)
- `backend/utils/db_queries.py` (new compute_group_status helper)
- Migrations: hand-written + idempotent (PMv2 has no Alembic)

items.title: Issue Correlation & Grouping
items.description:
Allow related issues to be linked beyond strict parent-child hierarchy.

Two primitives:
1. **Issue ↔ Issue typed relations** (m2m): RELATES_TO, DUPLICATES, BLOCKS, IS_BLOCKED_BY, CAUSED_BY, CAUSES, IS_DUPLICATED_BY. Wire up the existing-but-unused IssueLink table at `backend/models/issue.py:158-174`.
2. **Issue Groups**: named clusters of N issues with computed aggregate status (group "complete" when all members reach COMPLETED_WAITING_QA). New entity, mirrors QATaskIssueLink shape.

**Why now**: today the only relation between issues is `parentId` (single hierarchy). When two bugs share a root cause but aren't strict parent-child, the tree gets fudged. CB-1945 (cascade hardening umbrella) is the live example — currently parented as a fake hierarchy.

**Design backed by**:
- Code Review for AI Agents v4 (association object pattern, p. 197 — Primitive Obsession rule)
- UI/UX Design Principles for AI Agents (p. 7 — grouped flat list, NOT graph widget per Miller's Law)
- Web Application Security for AI Agents (p. 8 — enum validation, mass-assignment protection)
- Supabase PostgreSQL Best Practices (p. 8 — N+1 avoidance, FK indexes mandatory on cascade)
- api-designer agent contract draft (5 endpoint groups, full payload + error model)

**Scope**: see child Epics. Migrates CB-1945/CB-1946/CB-1954 fake umbrella to a real group at the end.

**Out of scope** (future features):
- Visual graph view of relation network
- AI-suggested groupings ("these N bugs look related")
- Cross-project relations

items.title: Implement parent-row lock across all 3 cascade walkers + concurrency test
items.description:
**Scope** (child of CB-1945)

Add a row-level lock on the parent BEFORE reading siblings, in all three cascade walkers in `backend/utils/db_queries.py`:

- `cascade_status_to_parents` (~line 585)
- `cascade_done_to_parents` (~line 800)
- `cascade_revert_to_parents` (~line 738)

**Implementation sketch**
```python
parent_result = await db.execute(
    select(Issue).where(Issue.id == parent_id).with_for_update()
)
```

Apply consistently across all three so the lock semantics are symmetric.

**Tests**
- New `test_cascade_concurrency.py` (or extend `test_cascade_status.py`): two `asyncio.gather` calls each PATCHing a different sibling under the same parent. Both must observe the SAME final parent state.
- All 12 existing cascade tests must still pass.

**Acceptance**
- All 3 cascade walkers use `with_for_update()` on the parent SELECT.
- New concurrency test passes.
- No regression in existing cascade tests.

**Why a separate TASK**
The CTE walk cleanup (CB-1946) is independent perf work; locking is the correctness fix. Splitting them lets each ship on its own merits.

items.title: ImplementationNote insert fails: NOT NULL constraint on updatedAt
items.description:
## Repro

POST /api/issues/{id}/documentation/notes returns 500 with sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError: NOT NULL constraint failed: ImplementationNote.updatedAt

## Root Cause

The Prisma-managed schema declares `updatedAt DATETIME NOT NULL` with no default. The SQLAlchemy model in backend/models/documentation.py uses `server_default=func.now()`, but server_default only takes effect at DDL creation. Since Prisma owns the schema, SQLAlchemy issues an INSERT that omits updatedAt — SQLite rejects it.

## Fix Options

(a) Add Python-side `default=datetime.utcnow` on createdAt/updatedAt for ImplementationNote, ExecutionSummary, FeatureDocumentation in backend/models/documentation.py so SQLAlchemy populates the column before INSERT.
(b) Add `@default(now())` to the Prisma schema and migrate.

Option (a) is the minimal fix — keeps the Prisma source of truth and unblocks API immediately.

## Surfaced By

CB-1609 regression test (POST a note via the new Add form). Also blocks CB-1606 QA verification of the create endpoint.

items.title: CRITICAL: AutoPilot task failure regresses completed sibling tasks back to IN_PROGRESS
items.description:
## Severity: CRITICAL — data integrity

When a task in the AutoPilot queue fails (exit code 143 / SIGTERM observed on CB-1585), some cascade logic resets **issues that had already been COMPLETED_WAITING_QA back to IN_PROGRESS**. Status regression is silent and bulk.

This is **worse than losing a single task** — it falsely reopens completed work, breaks QA tracking, and skews velocity / progress reporting. If a user has 100 issues in COMPLETED_WAITING_QA and one new task fails, all 100 may regress.

## Reproduction (confirmed 2026-04-30 on CB-1578 AutoPilot run)
1. Run AutoPilot on a feature with multiple tasks
2. Tasks CB-1581 → CB-1583 complete successfully (status COMPLETED_WAITING_QA)
3. Task CB-1585 fails with exit code 143 (SIGTERM — AutoPilot/Claude killed mid-run)
4. **Observed**: CB-1581, CB-1583 (and others) regress from COMPLETED_WAITING_QA back to IN_PROGRESS
5. **Expected**: failed task is marked failed; previously-completed tasks remain COMPLETED_WAITING_QA

## Suspected code paths (where to investigate)
- `backend/services/autopilot_service.py` — failure handler may re-mark queue items as IN_PROGRESS for retry
- `backend/services/autopilot_queue_service.py` — same
- `backend/services/terminal_service.py` — exit-code-143 handling path; does it call `cascade_status_to_parents` or bulk update?
- `backend/utils/db_queries.py::cascade_in_progress_to_parents` — should only cascade UP, never reset descendants
- `backend/api/execution.py::complete_execution` failure path

## Required fix
1. Identify the bulk update / cascade that flips COMPLETED_WAITING_QA → IN_PROGRESS on failure
2. Constrain the cascade to **only the failed task** (not its siblings, not previously-completed tasks)
3. Add a SQL-level guard: bulk updates that lower status (e.g. COMPLETED_WAITING_QA → IN_PROGRESS) should be explicit and logged, never implicit
4. Audit log entry for any status regression so the user can reconstruct what happened

## Blast radius today
Need to query DB and identify which CB-15xx issues regressed during the CB-1578 AutoPilot run. Likely candidates: anything completed earlier in the queue (CB-1581/1583) that's now back in IN_PROGRESS instead of COMPLETED_WAITING_QA.

## Recovery
Once root cause is fixed:
- Re-transition the regressed issues back to COMPLETED_WAITING_QA (we know the safe pattern: BACKLOG → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED_WAITING_QA per memory note)
- Add a regression test: AutoPilot with one failing task in middle of queue must NOT regress other tasks

## Do not
Do NOT investigate / fix while AutoPilot is currently running. Wait until queue is stopped. Backend restart will be needed for any service-layer fix.

items.title: AutoPilot pause-and-resume on token exhaustion
items.description:
## Need
When AutoPilot is mid-queue and Anthropic API rate-limit / quota / credits exhaust, the queue should **pause** rather than fail individual tasks. When credits return (5h reset window for Pro/Max plans, or user adds funds for API), it should **auto-resume** from where it stopped.

Today: token-exhausted state shows the dialog (Wait / Switch Model / Abort) but there's no automated resume — user has to manually click after waiting, and there's no persistent state across frontend restarts.

## Required behaviour
1. Detect token-exhausted error from `claude -p` output (Anthropic returns specific 429 + reset header)
2. **Pause** the AutoPilot queue — current task stays IN_PROGRESS, queue does not advance
3. Persist queue state server-side (not just frontend) so it survives backend restart / browser close
4. **Wait window**: poll for token reset OR allow manual resume via UI
5. **Auto-resume**: when reset detected (or manual trigger), continue from the paused task
6. **Switch-model** path: still works as today (Claude → GPT / Ollama / etc.)
7. **Abort** path: still works (cleanly cancel queue, mark partial work)

## Implementation surface (rough)
- Backend: `backend/services/autopilot_service.py` + `autopilot_queue_service.py` — add `paused_until` / `resume_at` columns or queue states
- Backend: `backend/services/terminal_service.py` — parse Anthropic 429 + `anthropic-ratelimit-tokens-reset` header, propagate up
- Frontend: `AutoPilotFloatingBar.tsx` already shows token-exhausted UI; wire to new backend state
- Frontend: `contexts/AutoPilotContext.tsx` — read pause state from backend SSE
- New: persistence layer (Postgres column on AutoPilotQueue table + restore on app boot)

## Test scenario
Run AutoPilot on 22-task feature; mid-flight, deliberately exhaust tokens; verify:
- Queue pauses cleanly (no half-completed tasks)
- State survives backend restart
- When tokens return, queue resumes from where it paused
- All 22 tasks complete

## Hierarchy
This is a FEATURE per the Jonny rule. Break it into:
- EPIC: token-exhaustion detection + queue pause
- EPIC: persistence + restore-on-boot
- EPIC: auto-resume on reset / manual resume UI
- EPIC: end-to-end test scenario

items.title: AutoPilot must follow Jonny's bible — bake discipline rules into project CLAUDE.md
items.description:
## Problem
AutoPilot subprocess sessions (`terminal_service.py` spawning `claude -p ...`) are fresh Claude Code sessions. They don't inherit the parent session's loaded skills (Jonny / Atlas). Result: AutoPilot can ship code without:
 - Filing a CodeBoard ticket BEFORE the work
 - Following FEATURE > EPIC > STORY > TASK > SUBTASK hierarchy
 - Running mandatory code-review + security-audit + QA gates
 - Transitioning items to COMPLETED_WAITING_QA on done (never DONE)

Reference: CB-1582 ran tests + audits but never planned a CodeBoard ticket first; never explicitly invoked Jonny rules. Worked here by luck. Could go off-rails on bigger refactors.

## Solution
Bake the discipline into the file every fresh Claude session loads automatically: **`<project>/CLAUDE.md`** (the brain file).

### Add a top-of-file section: "MANDATORY: Execution Discipline"
1. **Plan first.** Before writing any code, file or update a CodeBoard ticket. Bug fixes = single BUG with resolution in description. Multi-file work = FEATURE > EPIC > STORY > TASK > SUBTASK.
2. **Hierarchy enforced.** Never create orphan TASKs at project root, never sibling TASKs under a BUG, never EPICs without a FEATURE parent.
3. **Bottom-up status transitions.** SUBTASK → TASK → STORY → EPIC → FEATURE. Force IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED_WAITING_QA. Never skip to DONE.
4. **Mandatory gates before COMPLETED_WAITING_QA**: code-review agent, security-auditor agent, full backend test suite. CRITICAL/HIGH findings must be fixed.
5. **Verify before claiming done.** Re-fetch the issue from CodeBoard to confirm status actually landed.
6. **Memory-first.** Save lessons to memory/ as you go, not at end of session.
7. **Don't experiment in production code paths.** Stash + branch first.
8. **Never bypass safety checks** (--no-verify, --dangerously-skip-permissions on prod data, etc.) without explicit user approval.

### Implementation
- File: `frontend/CLAUDE.md` ... actually `/Volumes/Seagate/Claude/ProjectsManagerWebV2Production/CLAUDE.md`
- Add section at the top so it's read first
- Keep existing content (project overview, conventions, AI execution architecture)

### Belt + suspenders
Also consider: prepend a discipline preamble to every AutoPilot prompt in `terminal_service.py` so even tasks where the subprocess skips reading CLAUDE.md still see the rules.

## Acceptance
- `<project>/CLAUDE.md` updated with mandatory execution discipline section at the top
- AutoPilot run on a fresh task demonstrates: ticket-first, hierarchy, gates, COMPLETED_WAITING_QA
- Optional: terminal_service.py prepends the discipline preamble to every claude -p prompt

## Do not
Do NOT implement while AutoPilot is currently running on CB-1578 (would risk frontend/backend disruption). Pick this up after AutoPilot floating bar disappears.

items.title: CodeBoard IN_PROGRESS column truncates list after CB-1581
items.description:

5. Sort order placing remaining tasks below the visible viewport with no scroll

## Where to look

- `frontend/components/codeboard/BoardView.tsx` — column composition + filtering
